I was hungry and you did not give me food, I was thirsty and you did not give me something to drink, I was a stranger and you did not welcome me, I was in prison and you did not visit me, I was sick and you did not visit me, so go. To the fire prepared for you before the foundations of the world.

And I say to the people of the right side: You have done these things to me, so go to the bliss prepared for you from before the foundation of the world.) Did these people enter the Fire except for their sins into which they committed? Did these people achieve bliss except through their beautiful deeds that they performed with God’s grace for them? So whoever says: Sin has been abolished, then he has lied, and he has contradicted the words of Christ, and he is one of the liars.

And he said: O people who are possessors of understanding and knowledge, since they attribute it to divinity, and consider it to be theology, And they make Him the Creator of all creation and their God. How did that justify it to you, and what is the evidence for it in your view?

Did the books of prophecies say that about him? Or did he say it about himself? Or did anyone say it about his students and those who transmitted it, who are the pillar and foundation of your religion and from whom you took the laws and Sunnahs? And whoever wrote the Gospel and explained it, he made clear throughout the Gospel, from his words, his address, and his commandments, in countless ways, that he A servant like you, raised with you, and sent from his Lord and your Lord, and He will reveal what He commanded concerning you, and narrate the like of that of His affair. His disciples and students described him to anyone who asked about him.

And in their words that he is a man who came from God Almighty and a prophet who has power and virtue, so you interpreted that as saying that he expressed his words on The meaning of humanity, and if he were as you say, he would have declared himself to be a god, just as he declared that he is a servant, but he did not mention it or He claimed it, nor did he call for it, nor did the books of the prophets before him claim it, nor did the books of his students, nor was it narrated on their authority, nor did the words of Gabriel oblige him. The one who gave it to Maryam, nor the saying of Yahya bin Zakaria.

He said: If you say: You have proven his divinity in that He raised the dead to life, healed the blind and the leper, and walked on water. And he ascended to heaven, and turned the water into wine, and multiplied a little. So it is necessary now to look at whoever did one of these things and make him an act. Lord and God, otherwise what is the difference?

For this reason, the book “The Book of Kings” tells that Elias revived the widow’s son, and that Elisha revived the son of the Israelite, and that “ Ezekiel “raised life to many people, but none of those whom we have mentioned by raising the dead was a god.

As for healing the blind, this Torah tells that Joseph healed the eye of his father Jacob after it had gone away, and this Moses cast down the staff. It became a serpent with eyes with which it could see, and he struck the sand with it and it became lice. Each one of them had eyes with which it could see, but there was not one. Among them is a god.

As for healing the leper, the book “The Book of Kings” tells that a man from among the Roman leaders who became leprosy left his country, intending to help him. Peace be upon him to heal him of his leprosy, so the book told that the man stood at Elisha’s door for days without permission, so it was said to Elisha: Indeed, at your door A man called “Naman,” and he is the most honorable of the Roman leaders. He suffers from leprosy, and he came to you to cure him of his illness. If you allowed him to come in to you, he did not. He gave him permission, and said to one of his companions: Go out to this man and say to him:

He immersed himself in the Jordan seven times, so the messenger informed Naaman of what Elisha had commanded him to do, so he did so, and the leprosy departed from him and he returned as a caravan. To his country, Al-Yasa’s servant followed him and made him think that Al-Yasa had sent him to him, asking him for money. The man was pleased with this and paid to The servant returned money and jewels, and then he returned and hid that and covered it.

Then he went to Elisha, and when he appeared before him, he said to him: You followed Naaman and made him believe such-and-such about me, and you took such-and-such from him. And you hid him in such and such a place, having done what you did to him, so that his leprosy may remain upon you and upon your descendants. So that servant had leprosy in the place.
He said: This ninth healed a leper, and the leprosy was healthy, and he is greater than what Christ, peace be upon him, did, and he did not do that. A god.

He said: As for your saying that he walked on water, the book of the Book of Kings tells that Elias, peace be upon him, walked to the Jordan and with him Elisha his disciple, so he took his turban and struck the Jordan with it, and the water dried up for it until he and Elisha walked on it, then he ascended into heaven. On a horse of light, and Elisha could see it, and he gave his turban to Elisha, and when Elisha returned to the Jordan, he struck the water with it, and it was troubled for him until he walked. Upon Him we will return, and neither of them was a god when he walked on the water, nor was Elias a god when he ascended to heaven.

He said: As for your saying that he turned the water into wine, this book of the Book of Kings tells that Elisha descended upon an Israelite woman. So she welcomed him and treated him kindly. When he wanted to leave, he said to her: Do you have anything to do? Then the woman said: O Prophet of God, my husband owes a huge debt, so if you feel that you should pray to God for us to pay off our debt, then do so.

Then Elisha said to her: Gather all the utensils you have, and borrow from your neighbors all the utensils you can. She did so, then he ordered her to fill the entire vessel with water and said: Leave it for this night. And he departed from her, and the woman appeared, and all that water had become oil, so they sold it and paid off their debt. Turning water into oil is an innovation. By turning it into wine, and Jesus was not a god by that.

As for your saying: Christ, peace be upon him, multiplied a little until many people ate a few small loaves of loaves, the book “The Book of Kings” tells that Elias went down with a widow woman, and the drought had spread among the people and the country was barren, and creation had died of hardship and distress, and the people were in distress, so he said To the widow: Do you have food? And the Almighty said: {Allah is only one God. Glory be to Him. He must have a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a disposer of affairs.} [An-Nisa: 171].

As God Almighty said: {And they have appointed partners for God among the jinn, and created them, and created for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glory be to Him, Most High, above what they describe.} [Al-An’am: 100]
And God Almighty said: {And say, “Praise be to God, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in dominion, and who has no guardian. “Greater” [Al-Isra: 111].
And God Almighty said about the believers: {And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth. Our Lord, You have not created this for nothing.} [Al Imran: 191].

And God Almighty said: {Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he might be a warner to the worlds - to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He has not taken a son nor He will have a partner in the kingdom, and He created everything and determined it with a precise determination.} [Al-Furqan: 1-2].

And the Almighty said: {God has not taken a son, nor is there with Him any god. Then every god would have taken away what He had created, and some of them had exalted themselves over others. Glory be to God for what He has created. They describe - Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, so He is exalted above what they associate with Him.} [Al-Mu’minun: 91-92].
And the Almighty said: {Indeed, they are part of their iniquity, so that they say, “The son of God,” but they are indeed liars.} [As-Saffat: 151].
And the Almighty said: {Say: He is God, one. God, the Eternal, He begets not, nor is He begotten, and there is no one equal to Him.} [Al-Ikhlas: 1]
Just as he abstained from giving birth, he abstained from giving birth to a child.

And God Almighty said: {And they say, “The Most Merciful has taken a son” - “You have certainly come to something terrible” - the heavens are almost torn apart from him, the earth is splitting open, and the mountains are falling down. Guidance - Indeed, they have called for the Most Merciful a son.} [Maryam: 88-91]

{And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take a son. - Indeed, everyone in the heavens and the earth except one who comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. - Indeed, He has numbered them and numbered them as a number. And they will all come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection} [Maryam: 92-95].
And God Almighty said: “Never will the Messiah disdain to be a servant of God, nor do the angels brought near” [An-Nisa’: 172].
And God Almighty said: {And He does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Does He command you to disbelief after you have submitted?} [Al Imran: 80].

And in the authentic hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “God Almighty says: The son of Adam has lied to me, and that should not befit him, and the son of Adam cursed me.” Adam, and that is not appropriate for him. As for his denial of Me, he said: How can He return me to the way He made me begin? And the beginning of creation is not more insignificant to Me than Him. Bring him back, and as for his cursing of me, he said: I have given birth to a son, and I am the One, the Eternal One, who did not give birth, nor was ever born, and there is no one equal to Him.”

And in the authentic hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he said: “No one is patient in the face of harm he hears from God. Indeed, they will appoint for him a son.” And a partner, and He provides for them and heals them.”
For this reason, Muadh bin Jabal used to say: Do not have mercy on the Christians, for they cursed God in a way that no human being has ever reviled.

Then this Qur’anic Hanafi law came and forbade speaking against God in the name of a son or son, in order to block the pretext. It also forbade Anyone prostrates to anyone other than God, even if it is as a greeting, just as it is forbidden for anyone to pray at sunrise and sunset, lest he resemble servants of God. The sun and the moon, and by closing the doors in which God gives God a partner and a child, it was more perfect than other laws, just as it blocked other things. Among the pretexts, such as its prohibition on low intoxicants; Because it leads to many things, the origins of the forbidden things about which God said:

{Say, “My Lord has only forbidden immoral acts, those of which are apparent and those that are concealed, and sin and transgression without right, and that you associate with God that which He has not sent down therewith.” authority, and that you say about God what you do not know” [Al-A’raf: 33].

Of what the laws of the prophets agreed upon, other than the prohibition of good things as a punishment, this came in the law of the Torah, not the law of the Qur’an, for God He made lawful for the nation of Muhammad the good things and forbade them the evil ones. Likewise, He perfected monotheism in all aspects and closed the doors of polytheism in all aspects. Faces: This law came with the agreement of the prophets on the obligation of monotheism and the prohibition of giving God a partner or a son.

So if what Christ, peace be upon him, meant by the Son was humanity, and he did not call the Divine Son a Son, and it was mentioned that the Son does not know the time, Thus it becomes clear that Christ is humanity alone, and that He does not know the Hour, and this is the truth, even if they say: What they mean by the Son is the Divinity. Or divinity and humanity, it follows from this that theology or divinity and humanity does not know the Hour and this is false.
It is a lie, and it also contradicts what they said.

This text from Christ, along with all his other texts and the texts of the prophets, indicated that the name of the Son is humanity alone, and that he does not know what God knows him, and this is clear in that he is a created being and not a creator, and this cannot be an address to humanity united with divinity without Theology, as some Christians interpret it, because everything that the divinity united with Christ taught was taught by humanity, and because humanity is not the To them, the Son is not the divinity that is united with Him. Rather, the name of the Son among them is the divinity, and for the sake of the union humanity entered into it, and because it did not It is proven only the knowledge of the Father alone. He did not exclude the knowledge of the eternal Son according to them, but rather denied the knowledge of anyone but the Father, and this is contradictory. Because they say it from every angle.

chapters.title: A chapter on continuing the response to the Christians with what Al-Hasan bin Ayyub said and then with the words of Ibn Al-Batriq
paragraphs: [Chapter: Continuing the response to the Christians with what Al-Hasan bin Ayyub said and then with the words of Ibn Al-Batriq]

Al-Hasan bin Ayyub said: And like this, when the man addressed him based on what was written in the Gospel and said to him: (O good one), he said: Not There is no good but God alone. He said: The same is true of his saying in the Gospel: (I did not come to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me). He said: If he had a theological will, as they say, he would not have said this, for he has invalidated what you claim about it.
He said: Moreover, you claim that Christ is the word of God, and of the power of God, not separate from Him, nor separate from Him, and you bear witness to Him in The Gospel by saying:

(He will ascend to heaven and sit at the right hand of his Father. He will judge people on the Day of Resurrection and reward them according to their deeds, and he will assume judgment among them. And God Almighty granted him that, since no one among His creation would see him in this world or in the hereafter. If this person sitting in government between the two worlds on the Day of Judgment, and He who is seated at the right hand of His Father, who is a self-standing person about whom there is no doubt, is the body that was on the earth alone. By Him is divinity. You have separated God, Blessed and Most High, from Him, and you have divided Him into two persons, one of them distinct from Him, by their meeting in heaven. The right hand of its companion, and this is disbelief and associating others with God Almighty, even if it is a body devoid of divinity, and it is the word, and it has returned to God. As it appeared from him, the rule of lordship that you ascribed to him has disappeared from him.

He said: And we ask you about one thing that we would like you to tell us about. It is the origin of what you have established of worshiping the three hypostases that return to With your claim to one essence, which is divinity, what is it? Where did you take it from? And who commanded you to do so? In which book was it revealed? And which prophet predicted it? Or what word of Christ do you call him in? Did you base your matter in this matter except on the words of Matthew, the disciple of Christ, peace be upon him, that he said to his disciples when he wanted to separate from them: (Go and baptize people in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.)

He said: This is a statement that carries its meaning if it is correct that he meant it by combining these words until they come together. The blessings of God and the blessing of His Prophet Christ and the Holy Spirit with which he supports the prophets and apostles. We may see you if you want to pray for one another. To some you said: May the prayer of so-and-so saint be with you. The meaning of prayer: supplication. The name of so-and-so is a prophet who helps you in your affairs.
And as God, Blessed and Most High, said: {O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you} [An-Nisa: 59]
He associates obedience with his Prophet and those in authority among the Muslims, so should we say that they are all gods?

He said: It may be possible for it to have a meaning that detracts from what is referred to without interpretation, if its meaning is not what we said, or for Christ to be upon it. Peace be upon him. He referred to what He knows best, so why do you judge that he referred to these names when he added them to God Almighty? Glory be to Him, they have become gods, and you have made hypostases for them. Every name has a hypostasis that belongs to it itself, and He is one person. And how did you account for what you associated with Him? مَعَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ بِالتَّأْوِيلِ الَّذِي لَا يَصِحُّ؟

And if you say that there are three hypostases, each one in itself, then you must necessarily acknowledge that each one of them is living, hearing, and all-seeing. Knowing, wise, alone in himself, just as they say about Christ, “He is seated at the right hand of His Father.” We see that you have taken the two hypostases that You talked to God about the fact that God is wise and living, so His wisdom is the Word, which is Christ, and His Spirit is the Holy Spirit, and this is one of the attributes God has many like them, for it is said: He is Wise, All-Knowing, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, Ever-Living, All-Powerful.

Likewise our Lord, Blessed and Most High, even if our attributes of Him do not match His attributes and do not reach the essence of His glory except by imitating His greatness. And His glory, majesty, and exaltation, so you dissolved His attributes, which are its meaning, and there is no other than Him, and you made Him hypostases for every one of life. Wisdom and all other attributes are like those of Him, and there is not a hypostasis of them that has an attribute except that it is possible, based on the analogy of your statement, that His attribute is the same as Him. If these hypostases are gods and every attribute is a god, and it is from His essence, then every attribute must be for each of the three. The Hypostasis is a God like Him, since He was from His essence, so the matter expands in that until He has no goal or end.
He said:

And if you say that there are three hypostases in heaven from an ancient essence, do you not have to acknowledge three gods, because the hypostases are persons? It is indicated and the punishment falls upon it. Otherwise, what is the argument when you mention in some of your arguments that it is three that refer to one other than separated or separated, and you liken them in their coming together and the appearance of what appears from them to the sun, and we see that you have adhered to the law of your faith. That Christ is God and man united, and that he ascends to heaven and sits at the right hand of his Father, and who sits at the right hand of his friend, is it not He is separated

Separated from him? How can this statement be valid as an analogy, or as a debt contract? You sometimes say it is combined, and sometimes it is separate, and what you likened it to of the sun, we have already explained the invalidity of the argument regarding it, and that it will not be Its measurement is the measurement to which you are attached.

However, we found you saying regarding the meaning of the Trinity: What called you to it is what you mentioned that the disciple “Matthew” told in the Gospel about Christ. Peace be upon him, when he said to his disciples: (Walk through the country, baptizing people in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit). And you thought about this saying with your minds, then you knew that what was meant by that was that when the existence of the world was proven, you knew that it had created, so you imagined it to be an existing thing, then you imagined it to be living, then speaking, because a thing is divided into living or non-living, and the living is divided into speaking. And there is no speaker.
And you knew by that that it is a living, speaking thing, so you established for it a life and speech other than that in the person, and they are the same in essence.
So we say to you about that: If a living person has life and speech, then tell us about him: Do you say that he is powerful, mighty, or powerless and humiliated?
So if you say: No, but He is Able and Mighty, then we say: Then prove to Him power and might, just as you have proven to Him life and wisdom.

So if you say: We are not obligated to do that, because He is Powerful by Himself, Mighty by Himself, we will say to you: Likewise, so say: He is Alive by Himself. And he speaks by himself, and with that you must invalidate the trinity, or prove the quincunx, otherwise what is the difference? And there is no difference.

Al-Hasan bin Ayyub also said: Whenever we contemplate with you the attribution of Christ, peace be upon him, to divinity and your worship of him with God, The direction to which you are going, and we asked you for evidence for that from your books. We have increased insight into the impossibility of that and your presentation of it from A statement is something that proves to you as proof, and nothing of your books bears witness to it for you. And we found the clearest thing that came in Christ and the validity of his command regarding What the disciple “Matthew” said: “When Jesus came to the land of Caesarea, he asked his disciples and said:

What do people say that I am the son of man? They said: Some of them say: You are John the Baptist, and others say: You are Jeremiah, or one of the prophets. Then Jesus said to them: What do you say? Then Simon of Cephas, who was their leader, answered him and said: You are the Messiah, the true Son of God. Then Christ answered him and said: Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, for he did not tell you
This is flesh and blood, but my Father is in heaven.

Luke told this news in his Gospel, saying: (Simon answered him and said: You are the anointed of God), and he did not say the Son of God, so these are words His chief disciple was in it, and what he said satisfied him.

And he said: He did not utter that except what God revealed to him in his heart, and we have never denied you that he is the Messiah of God, nor that he is as You say in your language that he is the Son of God by mercy and by virtue, despite this difference that occurs in that in the two Gospels, and he said, for example: This is among you all: (Indeed, God is my God and your God and my father and your father), so we will work on your argument that there is no one like you in the meaning of prophecy. And we make him like someone who is named in the books a son, based on selection and love, like Israel and others. Rather, he singled out Israel by saying: God Almighty said:

(You are my firstborn son.) These are words that have a doctrine in the ancient language in which the books came, and they are not according to divine obligation, since he shared this with him. He changed the name, so why not make him as he made himself?

What confirms the meaning in this matter and removes the interpretation of those who interpret it as something that he did not claim or be satisfied with, is his saying in the knowledge of the Hour: (Indeed That is something that no one of creation, nor the angels who are close to Him, knows, nor does the Son, meaning Himself, except the Father alone.) Then he said to the man He who came to him and said to him: “O righteous scholar, which deed is best for me, which will be for me life until the Day of Judgment?” So he said to him: Why do you call me good?
There is no one who is righteous but God alone.” So he acknowledged to God that He is One, with no partner, and denied himself and did not make her nor any of the creation Welcome to that.
And he said to the woman who came to him and said: (Are you that prophet whose coming we were waiting for?

Then Christ said to her: You have spoken the truth, blessed are you. Then he said to Satan, when he tested him, and forced him to throw himself from the top of the temple, so he said: (We are commanded not to tempt the Lord.) Then he ordered him to prostrate to Him and said: (We are commanded not to prostrate to anyone but God alone, and to worship no one but Him.) Then his prayer at a time other than for God’s sake, the last of which was the night in which the Jews took him. If He is a god as you claimed, then to whom was he praying? And he prostrates?

Then what the crowds who were with him when he entered Jerusalem, which is the city of Jerusalem on the donkey, said to those who were asking him about his matter. The city rejoiced about him: (This is Jesus of Nazareth, the prophet from Nazareth)? Then he said in some of the Gospel: (Take us out of this city, for the Prophet is not revered in his city). In another place, he said: (A prophet is not disgraced except in his city, his home, and his relatives).

And he said in some of his sermons: “This evil generation wants a sign and it will not be given except the sign of Jonah, just as Jonah was for the people of Nineveh”: So shall the Son of Man be to this generation. The men of Nineveh rise up in judgment with this generation, and they contend with them, because they repented of the saying Jonah the Prophet, and indeed here is better than Jonah.)

Then David said in his prophecy against him: (Who is this man whom you mentioned and made him a little lower than the angels?) Then his disciples said about him what we explained in the beginning of our book above, and they described him as a man who came from God with the hands of God. And strength.

Something similar to this is that when he brought his disciples and they boarded the boat, he said to them: “Go, for I will catch up with you.” Then he came to them walking on the sea. When they saw him in that state, they said, “What a shame.” They cried out because of the drowning, and Jesus said to them, “Be at ease, and do not be afraid. It is I.” Then Simeon of Cephas answered him and said to him: O Lord, if it is you, then permit me to come to you on the water. And he said to him: Come. So Simon went down to the water. To walk on him, but he was unable and he began to sink, so he cried out and said, “Lord, help me.” So Jesus stretched out his hand and took him and said to him, “Why did you doubt?” Oh, you are so dishonest?)

He said: Thus it became clear that Christ was unable to complete what Simeon of Cephas asked of him, and likewise the matter of the man who told Jesus about his daughter and what He obtained it from Satan, and that he presented it to his disciples, but they were not able to cast him out, and he had assigned that and other things to them. So he took him out of it.

He said in the Gospel, while he was mentioning the parables that he gave to the chief priests, that when they heard them from him, they knew that it was about them. They were about to take him, then they separated from the crowd, because they were putting him down like the prophet.

And he said in the Bible, when the mother of Zenda’s sons came to him, and she was one of his students with her two sons, and he said to her: (What do you want? She said: I want to Thou shalt make my sons sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left, in thy kingdom. And he said: There is no way to that, for it is not mine to give it; مَنْ وُعِدَ لَهُ مِنْ أَبِي) .

Al-Hasan bin Ayyub said: O these people, nothing is more eloquent, clearer, and clearer than the collection of these pieces of evidence for you in your books. Did you accept what he said about himself, nor with what his disciples said about him, nor with the words of the prophets who prophesied about him, nor with the words of his crowd who They entrusted it to whomever of their opponents asked them about it, and you left all of that.

And you took the opinions of people who interpreted it for you, knowing that they also differed in opinion, so each people said in Christ what they chose. Each of them followed a group, saying what they said, then those after them followed the path of the fathers in imitating them.
So explain to us your proof for that, and that is no proof, and we ask God for protection and success from Him.

He said: Similar to what was mentioned above, what he said to his disciples in the Gospel of Luke 55: (But as for you who were patient with me in my trials and temptations, I I promise you as my Father promised me that you will eat and drink with me at my table in my kingdom.) It is clear that God - glory be to Him, has promised that He places him in the kingdom of heaven, eating and drinking with his disciples at his table. This is something you have no doubt about, and it is contrary to what you say regarding He goes to him, and there is eating, drinking, and enjoyment there. Then he says to Simeon when the crowds came to him and took him:

Or do you think that I am not able to pray to my Father, and that he raise up for me twelve armies of his angels or more? But how will the Scriptures be fulfilled? This is how it should be), and he did not say: I am able to repel them from myself, nor that I command the angels to withhold them from me, as He says: He who has power and authority.
He said: And we find you saying about Christ, peace be upon him:

He is eternally begotten of His Father, and the one who claims the statement must prove the evidence regarding it and know that he is required to explain it, especially In such a venerable speech, which cannot be tampered with, and no souls dare to raise suspicions about it, and long woe to those who misinterpret it. That is an interpretation that has no truth, for it will destroy himself and whoever was with him who followed what he said, if this Son was eternal. What is in the law of your faith? This is not by a begotten person, and if he is begotten, then he is not eternal. Because the name of eternity applies only to one who has no beginning or last.
The meaning of the newborn is that it is an event and an effect, and every effect has a first, so whatever you want to say about it is the invalidity of the Sharia.

He said: We also ask you about one thing: Why do you call the father father and the son son? For if it was obligatory for the father to have the paternal name due to his antiquity, then the son also deserves this particular name, since he was as ancient as him, even if The father was a great scholar, so he is also a great scholar. The law of faith bears witness to this in its saying: He created all creatures and they were perfected. At His hand, and that He came down for your salvation, and whoever is able to do that is only a mighty scholar. These meanings that we mentioned invalidate the name Paternity and sonship, and in invalidating them, is the invalidation of the Sharia, which says:

He was born of his father. Otherwise, if the father and the son are equal in stature and power, then what authority and authority does the father have over his affairs? And he forbade it, so the father became a sender and the son was sent, and the father became an obedient follower and the son an obedient follower? .

What attests to the validity of our statement and the invalidity of what your predecessors interpreted regarding the slavery of Christ, is that “Matthew,” the disciple, when he composed his book of the Gospel The first thing he began with was to say: The book of the birth of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham, so he attributed it to those of him who were authentic, and he did not He says: He is the Son of God, nor is He a god from a god, as they say: So if you say:

The naming of Jesus to the humanity that you have made is an argument between you and everyone who sought an argument from you when you stopped in what he confessed. For Christ from slavery, he rhymed “Matthew” after the name Jesus, which is a name for the humanity, Christ, who combines humanity and divinity. What argument to invalidate this interpretation is clearer than this? .
What confirms our statement and confirms it is what Angel Gabriel said to Mary when he was addressing her: He is the son of David, according to what was proven of that in The Gospel.

He said: We found you mentioned in the law of faith that Jesus Christ is the firstborn of creation. If you believed in that that Something like what is called the first born of a man and the eldest of them is permissible, and he fulfills our statement regarding his servitude, even if you wanted to mention the firstborn. It is an ancient first, so we do not know a meaning for “firstborn” in any language except for the eldest of the brothers and the first of the offspring, and firstborn. Creatures are only among creatures.

Just as the firstborn of a man and a woman can only be of their own kind, and the firstborn of fruits can only be fruit, and because it is impossible to say Someone said: The firstborn of Adam’s children was one of the angels. Likewise, it is impossible for the firstborn of created things not to be made, and the firstborn of creatures not to be made. With a creature.

God Almighty said in the Torah: (O my son, my firstborn), meaning Israel, and He said in another place: (Indeed, the sons of God looked at the daughters of people. So they became passionate about them.) Does this mean that the people of Israel are divine?

He said: And you said: Christ was born of his father before the worlds and not by something made, so the father is not devoid of having begot something that exists or It does not exist, and if it still exists, then the father did not give birth to anything. And if it does not exist, but it is something that happened, then it did not happen, then it is A created being, as we said.

He said: What clarifies our statement regarding the creation of the Messiah is that this name was only given to him, because he was anointed for prophecy and goodness, and God, Blessed and Exalted, anointed him. And God Almighty, David said in his Psalms a statement that testifies to that with his own eyes: (For this righteousness, God your God has anointed you more than He has anointed you. With it are your peers.) So David explained with this verse the meaning of being anointed with his Gospel, and that God his God anointed him, and that he is an honored chosen one. In addition to his counterparts, David also said in Psalm thirty-one, addressing God: (For the sake of David, your servant will not prevail against Your Anointed One.

“The Lord made a covenant with David of truth, and He will not turn from it.” He means his anointed himself, because God anointed him for prophecy and kingdom, and He said a parable This is in more than one place in his Psalms, so he called himself the Messiah of God.
He said:

And if he looked at the Gospel and the writings of Paul and others that Christians use as evidence, he found about twenty thousand verses that contain the name of Christ. They all speak of the servitude of Christ, and that he is a welcomed messenger, and that God has singled him out for blessings, except for a few verses that may cause problems. Each group of those who framed the Sharia interpreted it by their own choice, as they pleased, so they adopted that corrupt interpretation, and most abandoned it. Whoever speaks about his servitude, if they had intended the truth, they would have rejected those simple, abnormal problems for which there is an interpretation other than They interpret it in relation to the many clear things that have become clear without interpretation, because the part must only be compared to the whole, and the evidence must be inferred. What was absent with what was present, and what was problematic with what appeared. Among those verses that are problematic are what we mentioned in
We wrote this book and explained its meaning and the argument for it, and that it is not as they interpreted it.

Among them is what is narrated about Christ, that he said: (I am sorry for my father), and Christ, peace be upon him, explained that and revealed it. “John” said in his Gospel: “Christ implored God about his disciples and said: O holy Lord, protect them in your name that you gave me.” That they also may be one thing, just as I am one thing, and just as you sent me into the world, so I also send them. Then he said After this also: I have bestowed on them of the glory which you gave me and bestowed upon me, that they also may be one thing, just as I am one thing. And you are in me)
He said: This means that he said: You are with me and you are for me, just as I am with my disciples and for them.

I said: Or he meant that through me you guided the creation and taught them, and I guide them and teach them. And the “ba” is for cascade, for God, through His Messengers, guided His servants and taught them, and the Messengers taught those who were absent from them by those present and from whom they conveyed, And His saying: That they may be one thing: He meant by it that their truth, their command, and their desire should be in agreement, and this is explained, and He said: That they may be one thing, Just as I am one thing, He requested for them something similar to what happened to Him and to His Lord.

This shows that his saying: Just as I am one thing, that is, I agree with you in your command, your prohibition, your love, and your satisfaction, did not mean by that a union Himself through Him, just as He did not want their selves to be united with one another, so He requested for them a similar agreement to the command of God that He had obtained. And His prohibition, His love, and His satisfaction.

He said: Or perhaps he was referring to a precise meaning that he did not know, except that it was invalid. In any case, with this statement, your interpretation is mixing it up. God Almighty said in theology by saying about His disciples that He is through them, just as His Father was through Him, because if it is interpreted, it will be interpreted in this sense that He He said in his description that he was his father, and that his father led him to participate in theology. He said something like this to his students, so it must be That they should be, on this scale, partners in the business, and this is not the case, and no one dares to say it.

He said: It is astonishing that a nation whose book, calling, and deity is one should cling to the command of Christ, peace be upon him, and his disciples. And His Gospel, His Sunnah, and His laws, and despite that, they differ greatly regarding it. Some of them say: He is a slave, and some of them say: He is a slave. He says: He is a god, and among them are those who say: He is a son, and among them are those who say: He is a hypostasis and a nature, and among them are those who say: He is two hypostases. And two natures.

And each of them declares his companion to be a disbeliever and says: The truth is in his hand, and each of them does not come from the Book with a clear argument by which to prove his claim, nor By measuring himself and interpreting it according to what is correct for him when debating, but in his religion and belief he returns to what he interpreted for him. Those who interpret, in what contradicts their Gospel and their Books, through their own desires and stubbornness from one another to another, so they associate God with the interpretation, and do not He has a partner, and they claim for him a son because of what they have done for themselves. Glory be to Him, how can he have a son?

Al-Hasan bin Ayyub said: We have explained the arguments for the invalidity of every statement of yours that you have based on the law of your faith, and we found some of you When they were examined about this, they would say: We have found most religions in which their people disagree, and they differ over various opinions that they adhere to, and each Some of them claim that what is right is in their hands.
This is also a form of poor choice, and hearts straying from their guidance and turning away from the path of truth.

The people of no religion differed regarding the belief of their deity, nor did they doubt it, nor did they differ in opinion regarding what they chose, except the people of different religions. Christianity only.
And everyone else differed in branches of the religion and its laws, such as the differences of the Jews in their holidays and Sunnahs, and such as Muslims differ in fate.
Some of them said it, and some of them rejected it.

And in favoring a group of the Companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, over their counterparts after their group agreed on their God, their worshipper, and their Creator, And God, the God of all creation, is One, without any partner or son.

Then they agreed after that on their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, without doubting him, and on the Qur’an and that it is the Book of God revealed to Muhammad is the Messenger and there is no disagreement about him.
If their agreement on these principles is correct, then everything else is a defect that does not cause disbelief and does not invalidate a religion.
The great affliction is the difference in what is worshipped.

If there were a people who did not know their god or religion, and then the religion of Christianity was presented to them, they would have to stop practicing it, since its people were They did not agree on anything about it.
Their differences in their articles and their contrast with what was in their books indicated its falsehood.

As for our statement in the chapter on monotheism, and our acknowledgment of the oneness of God Almighty and our denial of partners, equals, and examples from Him, And the children, it is a statement whose veracity they do not doubt, and none of the People of the Book and other sects, nor any other people of opinion, doubt it. Of eternity and all other idolaters and idolaters, and each of them acknowledges it and returns to it.

However, some of them follow us in defining monotheism. And among them are those who introduce defects into it, by saying: Three go back to one, and an idol that we worship out of reverence to God, to bring us closer to our Lord. And His Lord, and the eternal Planner of things, we must acknowledge Him as their Creator and Creator.
And each of them acknowledges our statement, and follows our doctrine in acknowledging God in the direction to which he is going, and that He is one and not His partner.
Our contract has been valid without a doubt from you, nor from any of the nations regarding it.
Not in any of it, but necessity leads you to acknowledge it and agree with us on it.

Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, for his success, and we ask Him to complete His bounty upon us, to continue His payment to us through His power, and to give us life. And He will cause us to die upon Islam, not as polytheists, nor deniers, nor changers. Indeed, He has power over all things, and He makes all things difficult for Him easy, and He is among those who fear Him. He feared him and sought what he had and did not deviate in his religion. He was compassionate and merciful. Oh.

I said: This is the last thing I wrote of the words of Al-Hasan bin Ayyub, and he was one of the venerable Christian scholars and told people about their sayings. Because of their saying, its narration is more correct than the narration of others.
He mentioned in his book a response to the rational and auditory arguments they use as evidence, and the auditory arguments that invalidate their statement. And the mentality is what shows this.

With that, we mention the words of those who transmitted their doctrines from their imams who conquered the religion of Christianity, and we mention what they mentioned of their arguments, Like the penguin,

After leaving Alexandria, he wrote his book, which he called “Nazm al-Jawhar,” and in it he mentioned the news of the Christians and their assemblies. And their differences, and the reason for their invention of what they did with his victory for the statement of ownership and the response to those who disagreed with them.

Saeed bin Al-Batriq, Patriarch of Alexandria, said in his well-known history among Christians, which he called “Nazm Al-Jawhar,” in which he mentioned The principle of creation, the histories of the prophets, kings, and nations, and the news of the Roman kings and the holders of the thrones in Rome and Constantinople. And others, and he described the religion of Christianity and the divisions of its people, and he is a monarchist. He responded to all the Christian sects when he mentioned the birth of Christ, prayers May God be upon him, and he was born during the reign of the Roman king Caesar, called Augustus, for forty-two years of his reign. He said: He reigned for fifty-six years.
He said: After him, his son Tiberius Caesar reigned in Rome, and Christ lived for fifteen years.

This Caesar had a friend called “Palateus” from a village on the shore of the sea below “Constantinople” and that is called the sea. Al-Situs” and for this reason he is called “Palateus of Nabataea.” So he appointed him ruler over the land of “Judah.”
He said: In fifteen years of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, this Yahya, son of Zacharias the Baptist, appeared and baptized the Jews in the Jordan. For the forgiveness of sins.
Then the Messiah came to Yahya bin Zakariya, and Yahya baptized him in the Jordan.
Our Lord Christ lived for thirty years, and he mentioned the story of the killing of Yahya, and the story of the crucifixion, known to Christians.
Until he said: And Pilate wrote to King Tiberius with the news of our Lord Christ and the many wonders that his disciples were doing. Healing the sick and reviving the dead.
He wanted to believe in our Lord Christ and show the religion of Christianity, but his companions did not follow him on that, and he reigned for twenty-two years. And six months.
He mentioned that during his time, the city of Tiberias, derived from his name, was built.

He said: After him, Caesar reigned for another four years and three months. He killed "Plate" and appointed a person who was harsh on the disciples of Christ, and he killed the chief of the martyrs and the deacons. He was stoned until he died.

He mentioned that the disciples, both Jews and Romans, faced severe hardship, and many of them were killed, and that this man died and a ruler after him Another Caesar, and in his time there was famine and pestilence, and in his time he wrote “Matthew” and explained his Gospel in Hebrew in the Holy House, and he explained it from Hebrew to Roman "John", the author of the Gospel.

He said: During the nine years of his reign, Mark, the author of the Gospel, was in the city of Alexandria calling on people to believe in Christ, and that The first person to be made patriarch of Alexandria, and he appointed with him twelve priests and ordered them, if the patriarch died, to They choose one of the twelve priests, and the twelve priests place their hands on his head and bless him and make him a patriarch, then They will choose a virtuous man as a priest and make him with them instead of the priest whom they had carefully appointed, so that he may be twelve forever.
Their establishment in Alexandria continued in this manner until the time of the thirteen hundred and eighteenth century.

Then the Patriarch of Alexandria, who was among the three hundred and eighteen, ordered them not to do this again, and prevented them from doing so. The bishops reconcile the patriarch. Rather, they choose a virtuous man from any country. If the patriarch dies, the bishops meet and reconcile the patriarch. Which country were these priests from, or from others?
So he dropped the first chapter on reforming the patriarchs, and made facilitating the reform of the patriarchs a section, then he was named the Turks. Alexandria is Baba, which means grandfather.

From Ananias, whom “Mark the Evangelist” reformed, to the eleven patriarchs in Alexandria, there was no bishop in the work of Egypt, and there was no The patriarchs before him appointed a bishop, and when the common people heard the bishops calling the patriarch a father, they said: If we call The bishop is a father, and the bishop calls the patriarch a father, so we must call the patriarch a father. That is, the grandfather, since he was our father’s father. The Patriarch of Alexandria was called from the time of “Heraclius” Pope, meaning the grandfather.
He said: “Mark” went out to “Burqa” calling on people to believe in the Lord Christ, and “Caesar” Claudius died, and his son “Naron” reigned after him. Thirteen years.
He said: He was the first to incite evil, calamity, and torment against the Christians.
He said: In his time, Peter, the chief of the Apostles, wrote the Gospel (the Gospel of Mark) about Mark in the city of Rome, and attributed it to Mark.

He said: In the era of this king, “Luke” wrote his Gospel in Romans to an honorable man from among the great Romans called “Phophila,” so he wrote to him Also the aparxis, which contains the news of the disciples.
Luke the Evangelist, the companion of Paul the Apostle, used to say in some of his letters that Luke the physician said: “Peace be upon you.”

And he said: Then Caesar took Peter and crucified him on his head, then killed him, because Peter had said to him: If you want to crucify me, crucify me. Downside down, lest I be like my Lord Christ, for he was crucified standing, and the Apostle Paul was beheaded with the sword.
Peter resided twenty-two years after the ascension of Christ.
He said: Mark was the author of the Gospel in Alexandria, and he gently called people to faith, so he stayed for seven years.

In the first year of the reign of Naron, Caesar, Mark was killed in Alexandria and his body was burned with fire. Several Caesars were mentioned after him. He mentioned that “Titus” destroyed the Holy House seventy years after Christ, after he besieged it and its people were afflicted with a great famine, and everyone who There were males and females among it, to the point that they were cutting open the bellies of pregnant women and hitting rocks with their children.
And he destroyed the city and the temple, and set it on fire. And he counted the slain in his hands, and they were three thousand by one thousand.

He mentioned several Caesars after that, and that he reigned over one of them for fifteen years. He was called: “Then Theanus,” and he was very harsh on The Jews, and that he had heard that the Christians say that Christ is their king, and that his kingdom is eternal.
He became very angry and ordered the killing of the Christians, and that there should not be a Christian in his kingdom.
John, the author of the Gospel, was there and heard about this. He was afraid and fled to Ephesus.
Then he ordered that they be honored and that no objection to them should be left.
Then Caesar reigned after him for another year and some more, then another king reigned after him for nineteen years, called “Trianus.”

He said: This king inflicted on the Christians a great calamity and long grief, and killed many martyrs. He killed the Patriarch of Antioch in Rome and killed He was the bishop of Jerusalem and its crucifixion, and he was one hundred and twenty years old. He ordered the Christians to be enslaved, as they had no religion or law.

Because of the extent to which the Christians were enslaved and the severity of the killing they were subjected to, the Romans had mercy on them, and the king’s ministers testified to him that the Christians were theirs. A law and a religion, and that it is not permissible for them to be enslaved, so refrain from harming them.

He said: In his time, “John” wrote his Gospel in Roman, on an island called “Temra,” from the land of the Romans, from the land of “Athens,” in the era of a man. One of the great Romans was a philosopher called “Momodus.”
He said: In that era, the Jews returned to the Holy House.

When they multiplied and the city was filled with them, they decided to make one of their own kings. The news reached Tiberius Caesar, and he sent a commander from among them. He led him with a great army to Jerusalem, and he killed countless Jews.

He said: A foreigner fighting in Babylon came out against this Caesar, and he himself went out to him, and a severe war broke out between them, and he was killed on both sides. A great creation, and Caesar was killed in the war.

Andrianus Caesar reigned after him for twenty years. He went out to that foreigner in Babylon and defeated him. He went to Egypt and received from him He inflicted severe hardship on the people of Egypt, and he led the people to worship idols and killed many Christians, and his son Elijah was afflicted with a physical ailment. He would travel to countries seeking a cure for his illness, and they described the Holy House to him.
When he arrived there, he saw it in ruins, with no one in it except a Christian church, so he ordered that the city be built and fortified with a strong fortress.

When the Jews heard this, they came from every country and every city, and it was only a short time before the city was filled with them, and when they were numerous, they became king over them. A king.

Then the news reached Elijah, son of Caesar Andreanus, and he sent one of his commanders to them with a large number of people. He besieged the city, and everyone died. There was hunger and thirst there, then he conquered it, killing countless Jews, demolishing the fortress, and devastating the city until he turned it into a desert.
He said: This is the last destruction of the Holy House, and some of the Jews fled to Egypt, to the Levant, to the mountains, and to the valley.

The king ordered that no Jew should live in the city, and that the Jews should be killed and eradicated, and that the Greeks should live in the city and build on The gate of the temple is a tower, and boards are placed on top of it and the name “King Elijah” is written on it, and that is from the eight years of his reign.
He said: Today the tower is at the gate of the city of Jerusalem, and it is called the Shrine of David.
He said: The Holy House has been called “Elijah” until this time.
From the first devastation that Titus devastated to this devastation is fifty-three years.
And the Holy House was filled with Greeks, and they saw the Christians coming to that dunghill where the grave was and the Christians. They would pray, but they prevented them from doing so.
The Greeks built a temple named after Venus on that dunghill, and none of the Christians were able to approach that place after that.
He said: Then “King Elijah” died, and “Antonius Caesar” reigned after him in Rome for twenty-two years.
He said: In the eleven years of his reign, he made Yehuda bishop of Jerusalem, where he resided for two years and died.
He said: From Jacob, the first bishop of Jerusalem, to Judea, the bishop of this Holy House, were the bishops who were appointed over the Holy House. Circumcised.
He mentioned that after this, another Caesar named “Mark” ruled for nineteen years, and that he caused the Christians great calamity and great sorrow. Many martyrs were martyred in his time.
He said: In his days there was severe famine and a great epidemic, and it did not rain for years, and the king and all the people of his kingdom were almost destroyed by Hunger.
So they asked the Christians to supplicate to their God, so they prayed, and God rained upon them a great rain, and the epidemic and drought lifted.
He said: And in his days there was Magnus the Wise in the land of the Greeks.
He said: Within five years of his reign, Loliathus became patriarch, and he was the first patriarch to reform the bishops in the work of Egypt. He appointed three Forty years old and he died.

chapters.title: A follow-up chapter on the story of Ibn al-Batriq’s words about the Christians and his discussion of that
paragraphs: [Chapter: Continuing the story of the penguin’s words about the Christians and discussing it in that]

He said: In that era, the Patriarch of Alexandria wrote to the Bishop of Jerusalem, the Patriarchs of Antioch, and the Patriarchs of Rome in a letter. The Christians’ Passover and their fasting, and how it is extracted from the Jews’ Passover, so they wrote many books about it as it is today.

He said: This is because after the ascension of our Lord Christ to heaven, when the Christians celebrated the Feast of the Epiphany the next day, they would fast for forty days. They break their fast as our Lord Jesus Christ did, because when our Lord Christ was baptized in the Jordan, he went out into the wilderness and stayed there fasting. For forty days, and when the Christians celebrated the Passover, they would celebrate the Passover themselves.
So these patriarchs set an account for the Passover so that the Christians would fast for forty days, and break their fast on the day of the Passover so that their joy would be complete. With that.

I said: It was reported about the Messiah that when he fasted forty days after baptism, and he was celebrating with the Jews on their festival, he did not celebrate afterward. His fasting, the Christians participated in that for a period of time, so they began to fast for forty days after immersion, which is the equivalent of baptism, and they celebrated the feast with the Jews. Eid.

Then, after this, they invented a change in fasting. They did not fast after the Epiphany, but rather they moved the fast to a time when their feast would coincide with the feast of the Epiphany. The Jews, so their feast will be with the Jewish feast, which is the Passover of Christ, and that will be the time of his resurrection from his grave.

He said: “King Mark Mark” died, and “Commodus Caesar” reigned after him in Rome for twelve years, and in his days he was in the land of the Greeks in the city of "Aphragamos", "Galen", the wise man and master of the medical profession.
Galen mentioned in his index of books that he raised King Commodus.

Galen mentioned in the first article of the book known as (The Book of Ethics of the Soul): that there was in the era of King Commodus a man It is said that “Paul” was sought by “King Commodus” to kill him, but he fled from him. He had two young men, and the king arrested them, and the king struck them. He asked them to direct him to their master, but they did not do so out of their own generosity, their brotherhood, and the intensity of their advocacy of their master. So he killed them.
And from Alexander to Paul there were five hundred and sixteen years, and that was in the ninth year of the reign of “Commodus Caesar,” so this What Galen mentioned.
He said: This was also in the days of the wise Democritus.

I said: This period is longer than what this “Saeed” mentioned, for he did not mention that Christ was here two hundred years, rather he mentioned up to The devastation lasted for one hundred and twenty-three years, and it was mentioned before by Democritus.

He said: During the ten years of his reign, the Persians appeared and conquered Babylon, and they invaded Persia, and Azadshir ibn Sasan took control of Babylon from The people of Istakhr, and he was the first king to rule over Persia for the second time.

He said: “Commodus Caesar,” king of Rome, died, and after him Caesar reigned for another three months, then another, and after him “Severus Caesar” reigned in Rome for seven. Ten years, and that was within four years of the reign of Azadsher.

This king was severe. He inflicted on the Christians a great calamity and great torment. He killed every scholar among them and killed many people. He was martyred in In his days, he created many Christians in every place, then he killed all the Christians who were in Egypt and Alexandria, and demolished the churches and built In Alexandria as a temple,
He called it the temple of the gods.

After him, Caesar, who was Antonius the Bald, reigned for six years, and Caesar reigned after him for the last thirteen years. The Christians were in his days. Calm and safety, and his mother loved Christians, and in his days the Patriarch of Alexandria was called “Pope,” meaning grandfather, and after him another Caesar reigned. Three years, and this inflicted on the Christians a long affliction and great sorrow, and killed many of them, and led the people to worship idols, and killed those who He attacked the bishops a lot and killed Peter of Antioch. When the bishop of Jerusalem heard about his killing, he fled and left the throne.
He said: This Caesar died in the second year of the reign of Bahram ibn Hormuz, and after him another Caesar reigned for three months, then another after him. Four years,
His name was “Gordianos,” and within three years of his reign, “Bahram ibn Hurmuz” died, and after him, “Bahram ibn Bahram” reigned over the Persians for nine years. Ten years.

In his days, a Persian man called “Mani” appeared, and he demonstrated the religion of Mani, and claimed that he was a prophet, so “Bahram bin Bahram” took him in. The king of the Persians divided it into two halves, and took from its companions and what he says were two hundred men, and he stuck their heads in the mud, bowed down, until they died. Upside down.
After this Caesar, “Philip,” Caesar, reigned in Rome for seven years, and he believed in the Lord Christ, and one of his commanders attacked him and killed him.

Then another Caesar, whose name was “Daqnus,” reigned after him, and he was “Dekyanus.” This was during the ten years of the reign of “Bahram bin Bahram,” and he met the Christians. He experienced long grief and severe torment, and he killed countless people, and many martyrs were martyred in his days. He was killed in Roman ways. Then he went to the city of Ephesus and built a great temple in its midst, and placed the idols in it, and commanded people to prostrate to the idols and sacrifice to them. Whoever did not do that will be put to death. He killed a large group of Christians in Ephesus, crucified them on the fortress, and took among the great sons of Ephesus. Seven young men of his own and his own clothing, and he gave them precedence over all those with him, and mentioned their names, the names of the Companions of the People of the Cave.

He said: These seven boys did not prostrate to idols, so they informed the king of their news, so he ordered their imprisonment, then he went out to some places and released them on their way until his return.

When he left the city, the young men took everything they had and gave it in alms. Then they went out to a great mountain called Gaos, east of Ephesus. There is a large cave in it, so they hid in the cave, and every day one of them disguised himself and entered the city, and heard what the people were saying in He would buy them food and come back and teach them.
So King Dikyanus came and asked about them, and he was told: They are hidden in Mount Jaws in the cave.
So the king ordered that the door of the cave be built over them so that they would die, and God caused drowsiness to fall upon them, so they slept like the dead.
One of his commanders took a copper plate and wrote on it their news and their story with King Dikyanus, and put the plate in a box. Copper buried him inside the cave and built the cave.

King Dikyanus Caesar died, and after him two Caesars reigned in Rome for two years, then another Caesar named Gaonius reigned for fifteen years. After him, Caesar lasted one year and died, and that was three years into the reign of Hormuz.

In the first year of this reign, “Paul” was made Patriarch of Antioch, and his name was called: “Paul of Shimashati.” He said: He is the one who invented a religion. “Polianism,” so those who follow his religion and those who support his opinion are called Polyannians.

He said: His statement was: That our Lord Christ created from divinity a human being like one of us in his essence, since the beginning of the Son from Mary And he was chosen to be a savior of the human essence, and divine grace accompanied him, and it settled in him with love and will, and for that reason سُمِّيَ: (ابْنُ اللَّهِ) .
He said: God is one essence, and one hypostasis, and we do not believe in the Word, nor in the Holy Spirit.

He said: After his death, thirteen bishops met in the city of Antioch and looked into the article of Paul, and they made a decision against this Shamashati. They cursed him, and they cursed whoever said what he said, and they left.
He said: After him, Caesar reigned for another six years, and his name was “Oragus Caesar.”
He said: The Christians in Alexandria in his days were praying in the tombs and in the houses out of fear of the Romans, and no Turks appeared. In Alexandria; lest they kill them.

When “Naroun” became patriarch, he appeared and continued to rule the Romans until he built the church of “Hanna” and “St. Mary” in Alexandria and reigned after him. Two Caesars, then a Caesar named “Pharus,” and that was during the nine years of the reign of “Sapor ibn Hormuz.” He was harsh towards the Christians. He killed the two martyrs, the brothers Cosman and Damian, and Digitianus reigned after him.

He said: From the destruction of the Holy House by Titus to the reign of Digitian, two hundred and six years, and from the birth of our Lord Christ to Dictianus "two hundred and seventy-six years, and from Alexander to Dictianus five hundred and ninety-five years, and from The Babylonian captivity to Dictian, one thousand three hundred and thirty-five years, and from David to Dictian, one thousand nine hundred. Forty-one years.

He said: “Diqitianus” reigned during the eleven years of the reign of “Sapor ibn Hormuz,” the king of the Persians, and two kings over the Byzantines reigned with him. Twenty-one years, and these people inflicted on the Christians a great affliction, long sorrow, painful torment, and severe distress that defies description. Murder, torture, and expropriation of property. They martyred thousands of martyrs and tortured Mary Girgis with various kinds of torture and killed him in Palestine. They killed "Mary Mina", "Mary Bocatar", "Eytamchus", "Mercurus" and others.
He said: Within ten years of their reign, “Peter” was made Patriarch of Alexandria. He resided for ten years and was killed.
Within twenty years of their reign, this patriarch Peter was beheaded in Alexandria.

He said: Peter had two disciples, the name of one of them was “Ashla” and the other was “Alexandros.” And there was a man in Alexandria called: Orius says: The Father alone is the individual God, and the Son is a created being, and He was (the Father) when the Son was not.

Then Peter the Patriarch said to his disciples: Christ cursed Arius, so be careful not to accept what he says, for I saw Christ split open in his sleep. The dress, so I said to him: O my master, who tore your dress? Then he said to me: “Arius,” so be careful not to receive him and let him enter the church with you, the church of God.
He said: Five years after the killing of Peter, Asheila was made Patriarch of Alexandria, where he remained for six months and died.
“Arius” had sought help from “Ashla” with his friends, and he thought that he had retracted that statement, so “Ashla” accepted him and took him in. The church and made him a priest.
He said: As for King Diktianus, he used to search for Christians and kill them.

While he was going in search of them, he came to a place called “Maltia.” Then God poured out His wrath upon him, and he fell into great illnesses and diseases. So great that his body melted, and worms were falling from his body to the ground, and his tongue fell from his palate and he died.

After him, two Caesars reigned. One of them ruled the East, the Levant, and the land of the Romans, and the other ruled Rome and the like. One of them was named Alanius, and the other “Maqtius” They were like wild lions attacking the Christians, and they inflicted on them calamity and evacuation and things that no one can describe, and they did to them what no one could describe. One of the kings before them would do it.
And Qustus, the father of Constantine, ruled with them over Byzantium.
He was a religious man who hated idols and loved Christians.

So Qustus went out to the region of the island and Edessa, and camped in one of the villages of Edessa called Kafarjath. He saw a woman there. She was called Helena, a beautiful woman. She was converted to Christianity at the hands of the Bishop of Edessa and learned to read books.
“Helena” gave birth to “Constantine,” and he was raised in “Edessa” and learned the Greek rules. He was a boy with a good face, who shunned evil, and was gentle and loving. For wisdom.

As for “Alanius,” he was a brutal and extremely valiant man. He hated the Christians very much, killed them often, loved women, and did not leave anything to the Christians. A virgin girl, but he took her, corrupted her, and killed her, and likewise his companions, and this is what they used to do to the Christians, and the Christians were in distress. Very severe with them.
News reached him about “Constantine” and that he was a calm boy, little in evil, and full of knowledge and goodness.
His wise men and astrologers told him that “Constantine” would become a great king, so he decided to kill him.
And “Constantine” learned of this, so he fled from “Edessa” and went to the city of “Bzantia” and came to his father, “Questus,” and delivered to him. The king.
A short while later, “Questus” died, and God inflicted great calamities on “Alanius,” the king, until his flesh was torn and wasted, and he remained cast down, unable to Someone should approach him.
People were amazed at what he achieved, and his enemies had mercy on him because of what happened to him.
Then he came back to himself and said: Perhaps this is what is wrong with me because I kill Christians.
So he wrote to all his workers to release the Christians from prison, to honor them and not to harm them, and to ask them to pray for him in Their prayers.
So the Christians prayed for the king and prayed for him, and God granted him well-being and he returned to better health and strength than before.
When he became healthy and strong, he returned to worse than he had been in.
He wrote to all his workers to kill the Christians, and that no Christians should live in his kingdom, nor should they live in any city or village of his.

Because of the large number of deaths, they were carried on wheels and thrown into seas and deserts, and Saint George and his brother were killed in the city. Cappadocia” and they were from its people, and he killed “Barbara”, and he mentioned a war that took place between him and “Sabur” when “Sabur” disguised himself and came to him in disguise And he knew him.

He said: As for “Mogestius,” he was evil to the people of Rome, and he enslaved everyone who was in Rome, especially the Christians, and he used to plunder Their property and kill their men, women and children.

When the people of Rome heard of the king of Constantine, and that he hated evil and loved good, and that the people of his kingdom were with him in calm. And in peace, the leaders of Rome wrote to “Constantine” asking him and imploring him to free them from the slavery of “Mostius,” an enemy. God.
When he read their books, he was greatly distressed and remained confused and did not know what to do.
While he was thinking, a cross of shining stars appeared to him at midday in the sky, written around it with the following word, “Conquer.”
He said to his companions: Did you see what I saw? They said: Yes.
From that time on, he believed in Christianity, six years after his father’s death.
So “Constantine” prepared himself and prepared to fight “Mocostius,” King of Rome, and he made a large cross of gold and placed it on his head. The item came out, asking for “Maqistius.”
When Mogestius heard that Constantine had died to fight him, he prepared for war and established a bridge over the river in front of Rome. He went out with all his companions to fight Constantine.

He saw someone he knew, but he did not see it, so he remained confused and said: Perhaps I took the wrong path, and perhaps this is another city.

Then he entered the city and paid the dirhams of what he had with him, on which was a picture of King Dakiyus. He was denounced, and they said: Perhaps he had stumbled upon a treasure. Then They said: Where did you get these dirhams, otherwise we will kill you? He did not speak to them.

The people shouted, and a large crowd gathered around him and spoke to him, but he did not speak to them. So they took him to the road to the city and he spoke to him, but he did not speak, so he threatened him. But he did not speak, so he came to the bishop of the city and spoke to him and intimidated him and said: If you do not speak to me and tell me where you got these dirhams, otherwise... I killed you.
But he refrained from speaking for fear of King Dhakios.
So they said to him: He died, and a group of kings reigned after him, so they beat him until the beating hurt him, so he informed them of his condition in full detail.
They said to him: “Dekyanos” died and many kings reigned after him, and the king today is “Theos the Great,” and the religion of Christianity appeared.
Then he walked with them to the cave, and they looked at its companions and the copper box in which was the lead newspaper, in which was written their story and their news.
Their astonishment increased, and they wrote to the king informing him of their news. So he rode and went to the city of Ephesus, where he looked at them and spoke to them.

And after three days, he entered them and found them dead, so he ordered that they be left in the cave and not come out, but that they be buried there and a building was built over them. A church, and it is called after their names, and a feast is celebrated every year on that day, and he departed for Constantinople.
He said: From the time the youths fled from Dhakyus to the cave until the time they appeared and died, there were one hundred and seven or nine. Forty years.
I said: This is one of the things he made a mistake about, for God Almighty informed that they remained in their cave for three hundred years, or more, for nine.

But some commentators claimed that this is the saying of some of the People of the Book, due to His saying: (God knows best how long they remained) and that is not the case, for God did not This is mentioned on the authority of the People of the Book, rather He mentioned it as a word from Him, the Almighty.

Saeed said: In his time, there was the story of “John,” nicknamed “Chrysostom,” leaving Constantinople and his son, “Theus,” taking over after him. The youngest was forty-two years old during the eleven years of Yazdegerd bin Bahram’s reign.
In his time, Nestorius, to whom the treatise on Nestorianism is attributed, was made Patriarch of Constantinople.
He said: “Nestorius” used to say: The Virgin Mary did not give birth to God in reality, and for this reason there were two.

One of them is God, born of the Father, and the other is man born of Mary, and this is the man who says: He is Christ through love, united with the Son of God, and it is said to him: God and the Son of God, not in reality, but rather a gift, and the agreement of the two names. And dignity is like one of the prophets.

Then his statement reached the Patriarch of Alexandria, and he denied it and wrote to him, criticizing his actions and words and exposing him to the corruption of what he was. And he asked him to return to the truth, and many letters passed between them, and Nestorius did not go back on his statement.

So he wrote to the Patriarch of Antioch, asking him to write to Nestorius and inform him of the ugliness of his actions, his opinion, and the corruption of his words. He asks him to return to the truth.
So he wrote to Nestorius saying that he did not return. They and Anna met together, and many letters passed between them, but he did not return.
So they wrote to the Patriarchs of Rome and Antioch and the Patriarch of Jerusalem to meet in the city of Ephesus to consider an article. Nestorius.”

Two hundred bishops gathered in the city, led by the Patriarch of Alexandria. The Patriarch of Antioch was late, so they did not wait for him and sent to “ Nestorius did not attend with them, so they looked into his statement and imposed a curse on him. They cursed him and banished him, and they confirmed that the Virgin Mary was the mother of God, and that Christ is true God and a known human being with two natures united in the hypostasis.

This is the opposite of love, because Nestorius used to say: Neutrality (that is, union): the agreement of the two sides. As for neutralization, that is, union The upright: it is to be one hypostasis of two natures.

When they cursed Nestorius, John, Patriarch of Antioch, came. When he found that they had cursed him before his presence, he became angry and said: You have wronged Nestorius. And you cursed him in vain,
He became fanatical with Nestorius, so he gathered the bishops who came with him, so he cut off the Patriarch of Alexandria and cut off the bishop of Ephesus.

When the companions of the Patriarch of Alexandria saw the ugliness of his deeds, great evil occurred among them, and they departed from Ephesus and became companions of the Patriarch Alexandria and the Levant were two parties, and Theos remained king until he made peace between them.

The Easterners wrote a document and confirmed in it the correct trust, and said in it: The holy Virgin Mary gave birth to the God of our Lord Jesus. Christ, who is with His Father in nature, and with people in humanity, and they acknowledged two natures, one face and one hypostasis, and they cursed “Nestorius.” They sent the newspaper to the Patriarch of Alexandria, who accepted the newspaper and responded to them by agreeing to that.
Some people said: When he accepted the sheet of the East, it seemed to him, but he did not accept two natures and one face.
Saeed bin Al-Batriq said: They are liars about that. Because his books speak of that.
Then he sent a copy of the Orientals newspaper to a group of bishops, informing them that the Orientals had returned to the faith, and that they were not Agreeing with Nestorius.

He said: From the Second Council to the one hundred and fifty bishops who gathered in the city of Constantine, and they cursed “Macedonius” to this council. The two hundred bishops gathered in Ephesus under Nestorius - fifty-one years.
He said: When Nestorius was exiled, he went to Egypt and resided in a village in Upper Egypt called Ikhim, where he died and was buried.

His article had become well known, and it was revived long after him by the “Abishop of Nisibis” in the era of Positian, King of the Romans, and Qubad. Ibn Fayrouz, king of Persia, spread it to the East. For this reason, the Nestorians increased in the East, especially the land of Persia in Iraq, Mosul, and Nisibin. And the Euphrates and the island.
