If the body of a human being is struck, the jinn suffers from the beating and screams and screams, and the pain of the beating comes out of him, as people have experienced from This is innumerable, and we have done so much of it that would be too long to describe.
So if the jinn’s characteristics and conditions change as he enters the human body, then what about the human soul?
To them, the union of divinity and humanity is more complete and complete than the union of the soul and the body.
With this union, would a rational person say that they are two substances, each of which has voluntary actions in which the other does not share it?

And they say - along with their statement in unity - that the one who used to pray and fast, supplicate and supplicate, speak and suffer, and was beaten and crucified, is The counterpart of the body, and the One who commands and forbids, and creates and provides, is the counterpart of the soul.

This is in addition to their saying: Mary gave birth to divinity along with humanity, and that he was united with it while he was alive, before his life, and at his death. And the body in all of this is like all the bodies of human beings. None of the characteristics of the Lord appeared in it at all, nor even after He brought forth the signs. For something similar and greater than this was done at the hands of the prophets, so this is the closest to their example, and its corruption has become apparent.
And farther away from it, and more corrupt, is their destruction of fire and iron.

It is known to everyone who has experience that if fire comes into contact with any animal, plant or metal body, such as The human body and other things, such as wood, reeds, cotton and other things, and such as iron, gold and silver, it changes that. The body and changes its characteristics from what they were, so it burns it, melts it, or softens it, and the fire mixed with it does not remain pure fire, but It also becomes impossible and changes.

So these people say: It is like when fire and iron are mixed, and they are all joined together, and they form one ember without the fire being changed. Until it becomes a heavy iron that cuts and cuts, and the iron has not changed and transformed until it becomes a fire that burns), false and distorted words, The ember is not pure iron, nor pure fire, but rather a third type.
And his saying: (Fire does not change until it becomes iron, nor does iron change until it becomes fire) - confusion.

Mixing does not include transubstantiation or change, like the mixing of two condensed substances that he described, such as water and wine, water and honey, And ghee and honey, and gold and paper, and copper and lead, he said about it: Wine is not wine, nor is water water after they are mixed. But they have all turned away from their essence, and have turned into something changing, and neither of them is the same, nor is any of them free from corruption. And the impossibility of his situation.

Then it will be said to him: This is the one in which you recognized corruption and impossibility, the wine in it did not become water, nor did the water in it become wine, so this is the source of the dispute. If fire does not become iron, and iron does not become fire, then this denial will not benefit you, and this does not prevent the transformation into a third type. Among the things that are impossible and corrupt, as I mentioned in the mixing of the two dense substances, is that it is known that whatever the fire mixed with and united with, it changed it. It distorted it and corrupted its original form, and the fire that is joined to it is not pure fire.

It is also known that the ember that you struck is an example of Christ, and you said: God and Jesus united like fire and iron, until they became an ember. It is known that if a burning ember is struck with a hammer, or placed in water, or extended, then these actions take place in the aggregate, and do not take place. On iron without fire, and no fire without iron.

It is necessary from that that what happened to Christ of beating and spitting in the face, and putting thorns on the head, and eating and drinking And worship, and walking and riding, and pregnancy and childbirth, and other things that happened to Christ, and death, either early or late when he descended. To the earth, and from the crucifixion - according to their saying - that all of this would come to Christ, who to them is a perfect God and a perfect man, without There is a difference between His divinity and His humanity, as is the case with what is done to an ember of fire, such as carrying, placing, striking with a hammer, stretching, and depicting it in a shape. Specific and throwing into the water, and other than that is the case with the total Jamarat, no rational person would say:
This is permissible with iron and not fire. Rather, it is permissible with the impossible ember of iron and fire, and of wood and fire, which is not iron. Purely,
Nor pure fire, nor pure iron, nor pure fire, but a third impossible essence of iron and fire, like everything else that is impossible by union. And mixing leads to a third reality.

There is no difference between the two things if they are united and mixed and become one thing, whether they are dense, or one is dense and the other is fine. In all of this, there must occur to each of them some change and impossibility that necessitates unity, and that the united one be mixed and complex. There is a third thing among them, which is not just one of them, nor is it the sum of each of them as it is.
Their saying: (Indeed, with the union, there is a perfect human being and a perfect God), are corrupt statements with known corruption and clear reasoning.

Whenever they give an example of Him, the example is an argument for the corruption of their statement. Rather, with the union, it is neither a perfect human being nor a perfect God, but rather a third thing. It is composed of a human being who transformed and changed, and a god who transformed and changed.

And if both of these are false - rather, the humanity of Christ remains and is perfect, as it was, and has not been transformed or changed, and the Lord of the worlds remains. With the attributes of His perfection, He was not transformed nor was He characterized by any of the characteristics of created beings, nor was He transformed from what He was before that - that was what they said. ظَاهِرَ الْفَسَادِ.

This is their second proverb that they set for God, where they likened Christ or God with man to the soul with the body, and likened him to fire with Iron, and this proverb is more corrupt and more apparent.

As for the third example - which is the representation of that with the sun with water and clay -: it is more corrupt, for they said, as mentioned above: (And the example of the sun Mixed with water, clay, and every moisture and sludge, it does not change and does not lose its light and its continuity and ablution. Mixed with all blackness, dirt, stench, and impurity.)

It is said: As for the body of the sun that is in the sky, it did not mix with anything of water and clay, nor was it united with it, nor was it dissolved in any of the faces, but rather between them. There is a distance that no one can estimate except God, and God - the Almighty - is more exalted, greater, and farther away than the mixing of mankind from the sun, water, and clay.

If the sun itself did not unite, nor mix, nor dissolve in water and clay, nor in any other created being, then the Lord of the worlds It is better for him to be free from union, mixing, and solitude with any of the created things.

But the sun's rays penetrate water, clay, air, and other things that the ray does, just as the rays of fire penetrate the earth and walls, even if The self-existent body of fire that was in the wick of the lamp was a self-existent substance, and its essence did not reside in any of that. Places.

The word light, light, and the like, means something that is illuminated by itself, such as the sun, the moon, and fire. The Almighty said: {It is He who made The sun is a light and the moon is a light} [Yunus: 5] And He said: {And We made a radiant lamp} [Al-Naba’: 13] And Glory be to Him called the sun a lamp and a light; Because it includes, along with illumination and radiance, heating and burning, it is more like fire, unlike the moon, for it does not contain it with illumination. Heat, for this reason He said: {He made the sun a radiance and the moon a light} [Yunus: 5]

What is meant here is that the word light, light, and the like means something enlightened, luminous, existing by itself, such as the sun and the moon. And fire, and what is meant by it is the ray that occurs because of that in the air and the earth. This second incident is a separate incident and is not the first. An adjective that is related to the first, but occurs because of it.
The ray, which is light and the light that occurs on water, clay, air, and other things, is an incident existing in something else, and it is not united with it. Not at all.

If this example was used by the Nestorians who say: (Humanity and divinity are two essences with two natures, one is replaced by the other), It would be a false representation, for the sun did not replace anything else, nor did its will and the will of others become one, as Nestorianism says. Its ray is connected to something else, and the ray occurs and is created by it.

When it is said: Whatever comes from the Lord of His light, His Holy Spirit, His guidance, His words, and His knowledge, dwells in the hearts of His prophets and the believers. His servants, and this was represented by the radiance touching the earth - it was closer to the intellects, and for this reason the Almighty said: {Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth, like His light is like a niche in which is a lamp - the lamp in a bottle} [Al-Nour: 35] Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: His light is like in the hearts of those who believe in this.

Likewise, when it is said: His light, guidance, or speech, and it is called a spirit, it dwells in the hearts of believers, then it is in this regard, and by God He called that a spirit, and God Almighty said: {And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book or faith is, but We have made it a light. We guide thereby whomsoever We will of Our servants, and indeed you guide to a straight path.} [Al-Shura: 52] And the Almighty said: {He casts the Spirit of His command upon whomsoever He wills. Of His servants} [Ghafir: 15]
And God Almighty said: {Those are He who wrote in their hearts faith and sustained them with a spirit from Him} [Al-Mujadila: 22]
What was stated in the previous books that the Spirit of God or the Holy Spirit dwells in the prophets and believers is true in this regard.
When it is said: The word of God dwells in the hearts of the readers, then it is true in this regard.

As for the soul of the one who supports the Lord, it is not conceivable that he himself will support anyone other than the Lord, but rather the attributes and symptoms of the created being are impossible. That he himself can support others.

Thus, it is impossible for the attributes of the sun that are based on it, such as its shape and rotation, and whatever light or other things that is created by it is impossible to create anything other than them, Likewise, if a fire is made of heat or light, it does not do anything else. Rather, if the fire is adjacent to air or other than air, then this happens. A heater other than the heat generated by the fire itself heats the air next to it, just as it heats the pot under which the fire is lit. It heats up, then the water in it heats up, even though the heat of the fire remains in it, the heat of the pot remains in it, and the heat of the water remains in it. Another heat that occurred in the water was not one of your figs, although it was caused by her, and the sex of heat combines all of that.

For this reason, Imam Ahmad mentioned on the authority of the predecessors that they disliked for anyone to speak about the permissibility of the Word of God among His servants, by denying or affirming. The word “solutions” is a general term that means a false meaning and a true meaning.

The word “permissible” came in the words of the prophets in the correct sense, so those in whose hearts there is deviation, such as the Christians and their like, interpreted it according to the meaning. Falsehood, and there were others who denied this name and all its meanings, and both matters are false.

We have mentioned that people say: You are in my heart, or You reside in my heart, and You are present in my heart, and so on, but they do not mean that in and of itself. It resided in him, but they want that his image, imitation, love, and remembrance of him resided in his heart, as examples of that have been mentioned above.

What is meant here is that if the Nestorians likened what they claim of union and solutions to a beam with clay, their representation would be false, so how? By the monarchy, those who are the greatest in falsehood and misguidance? So their saying: (And the likeness of the sun mixed with clay and water and every moisture and sludge) is a false representation in many respects, including: that the sun itself It was not united or dissolved by anything else, but that is its radiance.
Among them is that the ray itself did not unite with the water and clay, but rather it came into contact with them and was created by it.

Among them: This is general to creatures in a way, and to His faithful servants in a way that is not specific to Christ, for all creatures They have in common that God created them with His will and power, and that they have no standing except through Him, and there is no power or strength except through Him, and they are all She is in need of Him, in need of Him even though He is in need of her, and for this reason it is one of the signs of His lordship and evidence of His divinity.

And whoever calls them manifestations and manifestations, meaning that his essence itself appears in them, then he is slandering God, and whoever wants by that to show It has His will, His power, His knowledge, and His wisdom. So he meant by appearances and scope what he meant by evidence and evidence, so he was correct.
The same applies when he says: These are His traces and the meaning of His names and attributes.

As for the believers, faith in God, His knowledge, His love, His light, and His guidance dwell in their hearts, and it is the highest ideal and example. Scientifically, Christ has no jurisdiction over this, and likewise His words in the hearts of His faithful servants, Christ has no jurisdiction over this.

Among them: that the beam did not mix with water and clay, nor did it mix with any of the objects, nor did it penetrate into it, nor unite with it, but rather it was on its surface. It is only apparent, but the beam heats whatever is in it, so if it heats that, it heats its surroundings, just as water is heated by the heat of a pot. Unless the fire has mixed with the pot or the water.
So where does this compare to their saying: (Indeed, the Lord of the worlds united with the son of a woman, and he became a complete God and a complete human being)?

Would a rational person say: The water and clay became a complete beam and a complete clay? Rather, the clay is clay, but the ray affected it by drying it out. The ray did not unite with it, did not penetrate into it, and did not settle within it.

This proverb is further from their doctrine than their representation of fire with iron, and their representation of the soul with the body, for there is a connection With the inside of the iron and the body, and here the beam did not connect except with the outside of the clay and other things.

Also, the soul is a substance existing on its own, and the ray is an accident. Likewise, fire is a substance. The sun here was not united and was not dissolved in clay, but rather Its rays, and the clay is not described by its union with the rays, nor by the rays being mixed with its interior, nor by the sun itself dwelling in it.

At that time, the one who said: (Indeed, the sun has not changed, and has not lost its light, its purity, and its ablution, despite its mixing with all filth and stench. And impure, if what is meant by it is the soul of the sun or its attributes that exist in it, then those are not united with anything else, nor do they reside in it, nor do they exist in anything else.
If the sun is like that - and God is the highest example - then it is more appropriate that he not be united with anything else, nor reside in it, nor be established by it.

And if I mean its rays, then its rays are not the sun, so imitating it will not benefit them, for they say: God Himself has united with Christ. And Christ - according to them - is the Lord of the worlds, although he is a perfect human being. He - according to them - is a perfect God, a perfect human being, and clay is not a perfect beam. There is no perfect clay, and the ray itself does not mix with anything, but rather it is mixed with it, and the incident is connected to the object without mixing with it, for the mixing is By mixing each of the two things with the other, such as mixing water with clay and the like.

As for what is attached to the apparent surface, it is said: It is mixed with all the parts, but the beam that is on the mountains and the sea is not said: It is mixed. For all the mountains and the sea, nor for the ray of fire: it is mixed with the walls and enters the earth, and it has been mentioned previously that they divided this section Three sections: One of them: mixing one thing with the other, such as water and wine.

The second: a connection without mixing, such as water and oil, and a vessel that is partly silver and partly gold, and they said: This is not It should be called a mixture with the separation of the two natures and textures, just as it should not be between water and the small amount in which it is. mixture ; Because the nature of pottery is not mixed with water.

This difference exists in the beam and the clay, and in fact the difference between them is greater than between water and smallness, for water is a body that exists on its own. This is a symptom that is connected to something else, and the body by the body is more similar to the body by the accident.
To them, God is mixed with all of Christ’s humanity, not a part of which was devoid of the union of God with him. So where does this fit in this?

When it is said: The ray did not separate from its light and purity and its ablution even though it was mixed with all blackness, dirt, stench, and impurity, it would not be an example. It matches it even though the ray is not mixed with anything else.

Then it is said: If he means that the same ray in the place does not change, then this is forbidden, because the ray changes by changing its place, so it is seen in Red is red, black is black, and blue is blue, so much so that when glass of different colors becomes the subject of radiation, it appears The beam is colored like glass, and is seen as red, blue, and yellow.

The people of atheism who believe in the unity of existence, and that the existence of the Creator is the existence of the created things, have set false examples for God, worse than The parables of the Christians, and they have an evil example, and God has the highest example, and among the parables they gave of God was that they likened Him to a ray in a glass.

The objects fixed in nothingness - according to them - are possible things, and the existence of the Truth determines them, so they likened its existence to a ray, and their objects With glass, and this is false in many ways: among them: the statement that the essence of possible things is fixed in nothingness is a false statement.
Among them: Their saying: The existence of the Creator is the same as the existence of the created being, is also false.
Among them: The solution of the ray in the glass requires the solution of one of them into the other, and they deny the solutions, and say: existence is one.
Among them: The ray that is on the same glass, its existence is not the existence of the glass, and for them the existence of God is not the existence of possible things.
Among them: The ray entering this glass is not the same as the ray entering the other glass, even if it is its counterpart, and these They believe that existence is one and the same, not multiple.

Among them: The ray is a display that lacks glass, so it lacks it just as the display lacks its place, so if they represent the Lord with it, it is necessary to The Lord is in need of everything else, even though everything else is independent of Him, and this is the heart of every truth, and the greatest disbelief in the Creator - the Most High - is - Glory be to Him - the One who is independent of everything else, and everything else is in need of Him.

And everyone who believes in God’s permissibility in any of the creatures, whether Christians or others, requires that it be in need of what has been permissible in it, for it does not There are no real solutions other than this.
For this reason, the faith, guidance, light, and knowledge that came to the hearts of the believers were lacking in the hearts of the believers, and could not exist without them.

And all the mental images that exist in the mind lack minds, they cannot exist without them, and the ray lacks its place, it cannot exist without them. Except for it, and so are all the other counterparts.

And these are the ones who imitated the Christians and added to their disbelief by saying: The existence of the Creator is the existence of every created being, and that He exists with certain beings. Those who are capable say: He lacks objects in His existence, and they lack Him in their steadfastness, so they make the Creator in need of all things. A created being, and the created thing needs the Creator, and they declare this, as some Christians declare, that divinity needs humanity, and humanity In need of theology.
It is known that God is free of everything else, and everything besides Him is in need of Him in every way. He is the Eternal One, the One who is free of everything, and everything. He lacks it.
So whoever says: He lacks a created being in some way, is a liar, slanderer, and an unbeliever. So what about the one who says: He lacks everything?

The example that they set for him requires that he be in need of others, and do not need others, just like the example that the Christians gave for him, when They represented it with a sunbeam and its place, for the place of the ray is independent of the ray, and the ray lacks its place.
The implication of this representation is that God is in need of man, and man is in need of God. God is exalted above what the wrongdoers say. Big.

{The seven heavens and the earth and everyone in them glorify Him, and there is nothing that does not glorify His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Forbearing. Forgiving} [Al-Isra: 44]

chapters.title: A chapter explaining that the general religion of Christians is not taken from Christ
paragraphs: [Chapter: Explaining that the general religion of Christians is not taken from Christ]

This is what was mentioned by this Turk, “Saeed bin Al-Bariq”, who was venerated by the Christians, who loved them, and was fanatical towards them when he told them about them. With which he explained their conditions in their religion, glorifying their religion, despite the addition in some of the reports to improve what they did, and many Some people deny this and disbelieve it, such as what he mentioned about the appearance of the cross, the debate with Arius, and other things. Many people He disagrees with what he mentioned. It is mentioned that the appearance of the cross was a result of deception, confusion, trickery, and deception. It is noteworthy that Arius never said:
Christ is the Creator.

But what is meant is that if this is true in what he mentioned, then it has made clear that the general religion that Christians follow is not taken from Christ. Rather, it is something that a group of them invented, and others differed from them in that, and that there was enmity and disagreement between them in their faith. And their laws are what confirms the Almighty’s saying: {And among those who said, “Indeed, we are Christians.” We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of that with which they had been reminded, so We were tempted. There will be enmity and hatred between them until the Day of Resurrection, and God will inform them of what they used to do. [Al-Maidah: 14]

The Christians acknowledge what this Turk mentioned, that the first king to demonstrate the Christian religion was Constantine, and that was after Christ. More than three hundred years, which is half the period between Christ and Muhammad - may God bless them and grant them peace - because it was six hundred years. Or six hundred and twenty.

If the Christians acknowledge that the faith they follow was created by a group of them while others disagreed with them, it is not quoted from Christ, and likewise what they are upon of permitting what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and likewise fighting those who disobey his religion and killing those who forbid pigs, Although the law of the Gospel contradicts this, as well as circumcision, and also the veneration of the cross.
They mentioned as their basis for this that “Constantine” saw an image of a starry cross.

It is known that this is not suitable for a law to be based on, as something like this happens to polytheists who worship idols and the stars. He is greater than him, and in this way the religion of the messengers was changed and people associated themselves with their Lord and worshiped idols. Satan imagines this And greater than him.

Likewise, the garment that whoever saw it saw, and the voice that he heard, is it permissible for a rational person to change the law of God with which His messengers were sent? What is greater than this? Although this is what they mentioned about “Peter,” the chief of the apostles, it does not include an analysis of everything that was forbidden, but rather he said: (What God has made clean, do not call unclean) Whatever God made unclean in the Torah, He made it unclean and did not purify it, unless the Messiah abolished it.
And the disciples did not permit them to eat pigs and other forbidden things, if what he said was infallible, as they think.

The Messiah did not make lawful everything that God forbade in the Torah, but rather he made lawful some of what was forbidden to them, and for this reason this was one of the influential descriptions in Fighting Christians, as God Almighty said: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow a religion.” The truth is from those who were given the Book until they were given the tribute out of hand, but they were humble.} [At-Tawbah: 29]

It was mentioned that some sects of Christians cursed each other in their seven assemblies and other than their assemblies, which would take a long time to describe, and his statement is true. God Almighty: {So We caused among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection} [Al-Ma’idah: 14]
At that time, their saying: (Whoever opposes Us, we will curse him) is useless talk, for every group of them is cursed and cursed.

Their cursing of those who disagreed with them does not mean establishing a truth nor nullifying a falsehood. Rather, the truth is established by the proofs and signs that the messengers brought. As God Almighty said: “The people were one nation, so God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warnings, and sent down with them the Book with truth to judge between the people concerning They differed over it, and none differed over it except those who were given it after the clear proofs had come to them, out of envy among themselves. So God guided those who believed when they differed over it. Of the truth by His permission, and God guides whomsoever He wills to a straight path} [Al-Baqarah: 213].

What was previously mentioned by “Saeed bin Al-Bariq” from their news is that the great Turks from among them used to come to a built church. For one of the idols that the polytheists worship, so he deceives them to make them worship in the place of the idol a creature greater than himself, such as an angel from among the angels. Or a prophet from among the prophets, as there was in Alexandria for the polytheists a church in which there was an idol named “Michael,” so the Christians made it a church. In the name of “Michael the King,” and they began to worship the king after they had previously worshiped the idol and sacrificed to it.

This is a transfer for them from associating themselves with a created being to associating them with a higher being. They used to build temples and place in them Idols with the names of planets, such as the sun, Venus, and so on.

Then the Christian innovators transferred them to the worship of some angels, or some prophets, and for this reason the Almighty said: {It is not for mankind that God gives him the Book, the wisdom, and the prophecy, then He says to the people, “Be my servants instead of God, but be divine in what you know.” The Scripture and what you used to study - nor does He command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Does He command you to disbelieve after you Muslims} [Al Imran: 79-80].

And the Almighty said: {Say, “Call upon those whom you have claimed besides Him, for they will not have the power to remove harm from you nor to transform it.” - Those whom they call seek to Their Lord is the means, whichever of them is nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is one to beware.} [Al-Isra: 56-57].

chapters.title: A chapter explaining that everything the author reported from Al-Hasan bin Ayyub and Ibn Al-Batriq is a response to the fact that Christ has two natures.
paragraphs: [Chapter: A statement that everything the author reported on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ayyub and Ibn Al-Batriq is merely a response to the fact that Christ has two natures.]

Through what we have mentioned, we have obtained the answer to their saying: (In this example, we say: There are two natures in the Lord Christ: a theological nature, which is The nature of the Word of God and His Spirit, and the human nature that was taken from the Virgin Mary and united with Him.)
It is known that this is one of the sayings of the Christians, and that they have other sayings that contradict this.

And each group of them considered the other to be unbelievers, as they were not based on an article they received about Christ and the apostles, but rather they were articles invented by those who He invented it among them, and they went astray thereby and were led astray, as God Almighty says: {O People of the Book, do not go to extremes in your religion other than the truth, and do not follow desires. A people who had gone astray before, and had misled many, and had gone astray from the right path.} [Al-Maeda: 77]
So, Glory be to Him, He mentioned that they were led astray by the sending of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.
The Christians are a nation bound by misguidance, the root of which is ignorance.

There is never a person who is a Christian, inwardly and outwardly, except that he is misguided and ignorant of his deity and the origins of his religion. He does not know whom he worships or What is worshiped with, along with the effort of those among them who strive in worship, asceticism, and good morals.

Then it is said about these: They say: (Two natures) and they also say: (He has two wills) and they also say: (He is a person whose number has not increased) For they say: (Indeed, they united) as they mentioned in this book of theirs, they do not say of two persons; So that they would not be forced to say that there are four hypostases.
Among them are those who say: (They are two substances), and among them are those who say: (One substance).

If they said: (It is one essence), then their statement would be like the statement of the Jacobites, especially since they say: (Mary gave birth to divinity.) And humanity, and Christ is a name that combines divinity and humanity, and he is a perfect God and a perfect human being.)

If it is one essence, then it follows that theology has transformed and changed, and likewise humanity, for if the two become one thing One, for that third thing is neither a pure human being, nor a pure God, but rather humanity and divinity combined in it, even though it was Man and God are two distinct entities, and in their terminology they are two essences. If the two essences become one essence and not two essences, then It is necessary that this third person is neither a pure God, nor a pure human being, nor are there two essences, man and God, for these are two essences. There is no single essence, but rather it is a third thing mixed, blended, and transformed from this and that, so the reality of divinity and the reality of humanity changed, until This became the third essence that is neither pure divinity nor pure humanity - like all that is known of the union.

If every two were united and became one substance, then there must be an impossibility in that, just as in the union of water, milk, wine, and everything else. It is mixed with water, unlike water and oil, for they are two substances as they were, but the oil sticks to the water and it floats on it and does not combine with it. Like the mixing of fire and iron, the iron changes from what it was, and for this reason, when it cools, it returns to what it was, and this is how the air unites with Water and dirt, until it turns into steam or dust and the like.
In summary, for all that people know about union, if the two become one and dualism rises, then the two must become impossible.
And when it is said: In it is the nature of the two and the will of the two, as in water and milk, the strength of the water and the strength of the milk.

It was said: It is necessary, however, for each force to change from what it was and for the other to be broken, as is known in all forms of union. If this is united with this, each of them will reduce the strength of the other.
Just as if cold water unites with hot water, the force of heat and the force of cold are reduced from what they were, so the united remains a medium level. Between pure cold and pure heat.
The same applies to water, milk, and other forms of union.

Accordingly, if it is united, the power, nature, and will of divinity must change from what they were, and the power and nature of humanity must be broken. And His will is different from what it was, and this unity remains a mixture of divinity and humanity, and this necessitates the lack of divinity from what it was. And the invalidity of his perfection, just as it necessitates the perfection of humanity as something that did not exist.

Everything with which they describe humanity, in terms of the union of divinity with it, entails a deficiency in divinity, the deprivation of its perfection that pertains to it, and the invalidity of His perfect attributes - according to what he acquired from that humanity by virtue of union. Otherwise, if divinity was as it was, then there is no union in any way. Faces, but humanity as it was.
Then they are two, neither of them united with the other, nor have they become one thing.

Also, since the essence is one, his will must be one and his nature one, for if he had two wills, he would have The place of one of the two wills, if it is the place of the other, and with the positive contradiction of the two wills, it is necessary for the two opposites to meet in one place.
The human will demands to eat and drink, to worship, to fast, and to pray.
Theology requires that he abstain from willing these things.
His will is to create, provide, and govern the world. Humanity prevents this will.

If the two wills and the two compulsions exist in one place, then that essence described as this and that must be desiring the thing. Abstaining from his will, not wanting it, hating the thing but not hating it, and that is a combination of the two opposites in multiple ways.

It is impossible for one description to be created by two firm wills for a thing and its opposite, or two firm hatreds for a thing or its opposite. Action does not occur except through a firm will with power, so divinity does not will it, and what it does not will, it does not happen, and whenever it wills something, it is a firm will. For He is Able to do whatever He wills.
Humanity does not do any of the characteristics of humanity until it firmly wants to do so.
Humanity refuses to will the will of divinity and hates it, so a single thing becomes a definite will for the thing, capable of it and not He wants it with a firm will, but he is incapable of it.

It is also necessary, if they are one essence and he was born, slapped, beaten, crucified, died, and suffered, that the same divinity be struck and crucified. He died and suffered, as the Jacobites say, and this is necessary for all Christians and is required by the doctrine of their faith.

If they said: Rather, they are two essences, despite the fact that for them they are one person in which there is no plurality, as those who say it from the kingdom say, it would be This is a contradictory statement, because a single person in whom there are no multiple entities is a single entity, and for this reason it is defined as a body.
If they liken this to the soul and the body, their time will be limited.

For man, as it is said of him: He is one person, it is said: He is one essence due to the union between them, and for this reason he is defined as a body. A completely sensitive person, moved by will, and speaking. This person has his body and his soul, and the soul and body have one will.
Whenever a person wills an action with a definite will, despite his ability to do it, there is no other substance with him that has a will other than his own will.
If they likened the union of divinity and humanity to this, it would require them to be one essence and one will, and this is what the Jacobites say.
For this reason, the soul suffers due to the pain that occurs in the body, and the body, which is the pineal heart, suffers due to the pain that occurs in the soul. The pain.

So, when the soul suffers, the heart of the body and other than the heart of the body suffers. Likewise, if the body suffers, and if the body is slapped, crucified, and spat in His face, and thorns were placed on him, and he suffered and died. All of this was a condition for the soul, and it suffered from him the humiliation of slapping and the pain of being removed. Just as they submit to God that he inhabited the soul and body of Christ, they do not dispute that God inhabited the body and soul of Christ, but rather They dispute over theology, even though the soul separates from the body at death.
Their divinity did not separate from humanity through death, but rather ascended to heaven.
Christ, who is perfect God and perfect man, will sit at the right hand of His Father, and the same will come on the Day of Resurrection.

Also, if the body is in it, its characteristics and rulings change, and its conditions differ as it comes together and separates, and the soul If it is in the body, its characteristics and rulings will differ.

It is necessary that the humanity of Christ be different in characteristics and rulings from all other humanity, and that the divinity of what was united with it was changed. His attributes and rulings, and this is the transubstantiation, change and change of the attributes, even though the humanity of Christ was of the same type as human beings. Not only did the likes of it appear on him, but the supernatural features of customs appeared on him more than what appeared on him.
In short, any example they set for unity was an argument against them and demonstrated the corruption of their words.

And if they say: This is something that does not make sense, rather it is beyond reason, the answer is from two sides: One of them: It is necessary to differentiate between what is known. The mind is its futility and impossibility, and what the mind is unable to imagine and know.
The first is one of the impossibilities of the mind, and the second is one of the impossibilities of the mind, and the messengers inform of the second.

As for the first: No one would say it except a liar, and if it were permissible to say this, it would be permissible to say: A single body is white and black in One state, that one thing exists in two places, that one thing exists and is non-existent in one state, and similar things. The mind knows its abstinence.
What the Christians say is something that is known to a clear mind to be false, not something that is impossible to imagine.

This clarifies that if someone said about Mary, the mother of Christ: (the wife of God and his wife), and that he had married her mentally, as They say: Christ was born of an intellectual birth. This statement was not more corrupted in the mind than their statement about the Messiah, as we have explained in Its place, and they consider whoever says that to be an unbeliever, and they use reason as evidence against its corruption.

And if he said: (This is beyond reason) they did not accept it, and likewise each of their sects protested against the other with reason. They said: (Our saying is beyond reason.) They did not accept this answer.

If this is a correct answer, then nothing of the divine matters should be investigated with reason. Rather, every false person says whatever he wants about falsehood. And he says: My words are beyond reason, as say the people of solution, unity and unity who say: The existence of the Creator is the existence of the created being. They say: This is beyond the mind, and that it is known by taste, not by hearing or reason.
The second aspect: That it is said: What the mind cannot imagine if the prophets - peace be upon them - informed of it, it was accepted from them; Because they know what others cannot know.
And the prophets did not say any of these sayings. Rather, the same groups of Christians said them with their own opinions, and they claimed that they derived them from Some words from the books.
So it will be said to whoever said it: Do you imagine what you are saying, or do you not imagine it, understand it, and rationalize it?

If he says: I cannot imagine what I am saying, nor understand it, nor understand it, it will be said to him: You have said about God what you do not know, and you have concealed what you do not have. Science.
One of the greatest sins forbidden in all laws is for a person to express his opinion about God in a way that he neither imagines nor understands.
All wise people know that whoever says a word without conceiving it or understanding it, then his statement will be rejected and not accepted from him. His statement is false and reprehensible.

And if their speaker says: I understand what I say and can imagine it and understand it, he will be told: Explain it to someone else so that he understands it and understands it. And imagine it, and do not say it is beyond the mind, rather it is a statement that you have rationalized and understood, and this is a division from which they cannot depart.
If they understand what they say and make sense of it, it must be reasonable.

And if they do not understand it nor understand it, it is necessary that they said about God what they neither understand nor understand in words according to their opinion. And their reason, not a copy of the words of the prophets, for whoever quotes the words of the prophets proven from them, does not have to understand jurisprudence. He makes sense of what he says.

For this reason, the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - said: “May God bless the person who heard a hadith from us and conveyed it to those who did not hear it. Perhaps he carries a jurisprudence other than A jurist, and perhaps one who will carry jurisprudence to those who are more knowledgeable than him.” A man may memorize a word and someone else conveys it to him, even though he neither understands its meaning nor understands it.
Whoever quotes a word from the Torah, the Gospel, the Qur’an, or the words of the other prophets, we do not ask him to explain its meaning.

Unlike the one who claimed that he understood what the prophets said, and expressed that in other words, it is said to him: If you understood what They said it, so it is one meaning. They expressed it with one expression and I expressed it with another expression, like the translators, so this makes sense of what he says. And he understands him.

And if he says: I did not understand what they said, or I did not understand what I said, then he has acknowledged his ignorance and misguidance, and that he is one of those who did not understand. The words of the prophets - peace be upon them - and they did not understand what they themselves said.
If they had said: We do not understand the words of the prophets and had remained silent, they would have been like their ilk who are ignorant of the meanings of the words of the prophets.

But if they created a phrase and a speech, they invented it, and commanded the people to believe it, and said: This is faith and monotheism, and said: We are with We cannot imagine what we said, nor understand it, nor understand it, for these are among those who say about God what they do not know, and they slander against God and against Him. The Books of God and the Prophets of God without knowledge. Rather, they speak fabricated lies and clear disbelief, and they say in addition to that: We do not understand it. This is undoubtedly the case with Christians.

In this situation, two groups of people made a mistake: the exaggerated, who went to extremes in the intelligible to the point that they made what was not intelligible into the intelligible, and put it before the senses. And the texts of the Messenger.
A group deviated from it, rejecting the clear intelligibles and preferring to them what they thought of the aural and sensory matters.
Thus there are two types of people regarding auditory matters, and similarly there are two types of people regarding internal and external senses.
It must be known that the truth does not contradict the other, but rather confirms the other.

Unlike falsehood, it is different and contradictory, as God Almighty said regarding those who dissent from the Messengers: {By the heaven that contains your love. Indeed, you are of differing speech. He will be spared from it whoever turns away from it.} [Al-Dhariyat: 7]
Whatever is known with reason and clarity, there is no contradiction with it at all, no news is correct or sense is correct.
Likewise, what is known by correct hearing is not contradicted by reason or sense.
The same applies to what is known by sound sense, which is not contradicted by any news or reason.
What is meant here is to talk to someone who opposes what is reasonable through hearing or feeling.
So we say: The word “reasonable” means the clear, reasonable thing that people know by the nature in which they were created, without some of them receiving it from others. some,

Just as they know the similarity of the similar and the difference of the different - I mean the difference of diversity, not the difference of contrast and contrast - the word (Difference) means this and that.

And these are the intelligible matters regarding processes and processes, which God condemned those who disobeyed them, saying: {And they say, “If we had only heard or reasoned, we would not have understood.” We were among the companions of the Blazing Fire.} [Al-Mulk: 10] And His saying: {Have they not traveled through the land and had hearts with which they reason, or ears with which they hear?} [Al-Hajj: 46]

As for what some people call (intelligibles) and many rational people disagree with them, such as the saying that bodies are similar and the symptoms remain, and that Bodies are composed of separate, indivisible substances, or of matter and form, and that the things are infinite. successive thing after something, its existence is impossible either in the past and the future, or in the past only, or that universals exist in External substances existing on their own, or that we have an age or matter that is an intellectual substance existing on its own, or that it is possible to exist A self-existent essence that cannot be referred to, and other things that those theorists consider to be rationalities.
Others dispute them about it.

These are not the intellects for which one should not reject sense and hearing, and upon which the knowledge of the children of Adam is built. Rather, they are the correct intelligibles. The hidden subtlety is attributed to primary intuitive concepts, in contrast to explicit rationalities, such as the fact that a single body does not exist in Two places at the same time together, for this is known by the nature of God with which He created people.

If there is something in sense or authentic news that is thought to be contrary to that, such as if a single person was seen in Arafat while he was in his own country, he would not He walks away, or he is seen sitting in his place while he is in another place, or he is seen helping those who sought his help, or he comes flying in the air with the knowledge That he is in his place and has not changed from him, so this is just a jinn that took the image of that person, it is not himself, so this He looks like him, not him.

And the sensory things, if one does not distinguish between them with the mind, otherwise the senses make many mistakes. Likewise, whoever claims about what he has achieved from revelation. Addressing someone is something that contradicts the clear mind and in which he knows that he is mistaken, such as someone who says of the oneness of existence: (I bear witness with my inner being) absolute existence, devoid of names and attributes,
There is no specification or restriction in it at all) so there is no dispute over this, as some people may dispute it.

But it will be said to him: From where did you know that this is the Lord of the worlds who created the heavens and the earth? The fact that what you witnessed with your heart is God is something that cannot be perceived by the sense of the heart, and if you claim that you have achieved in the revelation something that is clearly contradictory Reason knows that you are wrong, as the sheikh of these atheists Al-Tilmisani said: Oh my friend, you forbid me and command me... and in reality I am more truthful. End and command, if I obey you and disobey my existence, I will return blind... from sight to illusions of information and knowledge of what you are calling me to if... you achieve In it you will see the prohibition, O neighbor, and it will be said to him:

Your presence and your taste did not benefit you except as witnesses of a simple absolute existence, but how did you know that this is the Lord of the worlds? Rather, how do you know that this is established outside of yourself, completely, absolutely, and abstractly? Rather, you witness it completely, absolutely, and abstractly in yourself.
And you do not know by sense, reason, or information that this is outside.
Likewise, when the sleeper witnesses his inner sense of things, he is not certain that this is outside.
When his mind returned to him, he knew that this was in his imagination in a dream.

The same goes for the drunkard and anyone else whose mind is weak. This person testifies to things through his inner or outer sense, and his mind has become weak from This was so when it came to him, and when his mind came to him, he would know that what he witnessed was within himself and his imagination, not outside of it. That.

Everyone who reports something that contradicts the authenticity of what has been reported or is clear about what is reasonable knows that he has made a mistake, even if he is truthful in what he witnesses in sense. The hidden or the apparent, but the mistake occurred in his corrupt opinion that was contrary to clear reason, and not in mere sense, for sense does not contain negative knowledge. Or proof.
Whoever sees a person, there is nothing in sense except his vision.

As for his being Zaid or Omar, there must be a mind to distinguish between this and that, and for this reason the young, the insane, and the demented were The drunkard, the sleeper, and the like - they have senses, but due to their lack of reason, they cannot distinguish whether what is witnessed is such-and-such or such-and-such. They have incorrect suspicions.

God Almighty said: {And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a valley, which the thirsty person thinks is water; until, when he comes to it, he does not find it to be anything, but he finds God with him. Then He paid him his account, and God is quick to account.” [An-Nour: 39].
The thirsty person sees that what he thought was water, but it was not water because he suspected it was water, and his senses were not mistaken, but his mind was wrong.
The prophets - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them - are infallible. They do not say anything about God except the truth, and they do not transmit anything from Him except the truth.
Whoever claims in their narrations something that contradicts what is clear and reasonable is a liar. Indeed, it must be that what is reasonable is not clear, or that The quote is not correct.
If it is known with certainty that they were informed, it is impossible for there to be anything in the mind that contradicts it.
And as long as it is known with certainty that reason has ruled it, it is impossible for there to be anything in their reports that contradicts it.

The statement of the people of unity among the Christians and others - whether they claim general or specific unity - is known with clear reason to be false, so it is impossible That a prophet from among the prophets would inform of it. Rather, the prophets - peace be upon them - may inform about what the mind is unable to know, not what The mind knows its falsity, so they are informed of the ambiguities of the minds, not the impossibilities of the minds.
Anyone other than the prophets is not infallible. He may make mistakes, and things may happen to him in his revelations, senses, tastes, and witnesses about which he is suspicious. False.
So if someone like this tells something - and he knows its falsehood with a clear mind - it is known that he is wrong.

If someone other than the prophets tells something that the mind of many people is unable to know, it is not necessary for him to be truthful or a liar. We judge whether it is truthful or false except with evidence. Because of the possibility that he was wrong and the possibility that he knew what others could not know.

And if he says a well-known statement, then it is invalidated by a clear-minded person who is not a prophet, and he says: This is beyond reason, or this is beyond a stage. Reason and transmission, or we do not know this if we do not abandon reason and transmission, or he said: They are a group that dissolved the system and burned the fence, so no It is an obligation for them, and the madmen do not do anything except that the secret of their madness is... Mighty, at its gates the mind prostrates. It was said: This is impossible to say. A prophet, or a truthful narration of it from a prophet, for the sayings of the prophets do not contradict clear reason, so how can this be accepted from someone who is not a prophet?
And if he says as the Christians or others say: This is indicated by the words of the prophets or we understood it from the words of the prophets.
It was said to them: Talking about the meanings of the words spoken by the prophets is one thing, and talking about the meanings of the words that the prophets uttered is another thing.

If it were assumed that what you or others mentioned and understood from the words of the prophets is not contrary to clear reason, we would not be certain that he said He may imagine what he said, but it may be that he understood from what they said what they did not want.

So how if he himself did not imagine what he said? Rather, they acknowledge that it is unreasonable to him, and he does not understand it, so how if what he said was known to be corrupt and of clear reason?
These are three premises: If he understood him, then said: I understood his words, his understanding would not be an argument.
So what if he said: I did not understand him, and this is beyond the stage of reason?

If he had said this, his statement would not have been proof, and he should not be believed because the prophets meant by their words the meaning that he acknowledged to be above. The development of reason, so how if it is known that that meaning is false and could not be said by a rational person, neither a prophet nor a non-prophet?

chapters.title: Separating the answer from the Christians’ suspicion of the Muslims’ acknowledgment of the attributes and that it does not require resemblance or anthropomorphism
paragraphs: [Chapter: The answer to the Christians’ suspicion regarding Muslims’ approval of attributes and that it does not require resemblance or anthropomorphism]

The narrator said about them: So I said to them: They say to us: If your belief in the Creator - the Almighty - is that He is one, then what motivated you to do so? You say: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, so you deceive the listeners that you believe in God three composite persons, or three gods, or three gods. Parts, and that he has a son, and those who do not know your belief think that you mean by this the son of intercourse and procreation, so you criticize Is there an accusation against yourselves of which you are innocent?
They said: And they too, since their belief in the Creator is that His greatness is that He is incorporeal, without limbs and organs, and is not limited to place, so what prompted them to say:

Indeed, he has eyes with which he sees, and two hands which he extends, and a leg and a face which he turns to every place, and a side, and he comes in shades of Clouds, so they give the listeners the illusion that God has a body and limbs and limbs, and that He moves from one place to another in shades of clouds. Those who do not know their belief think that they anthropomorphize the Creator, to the point that some of them believed that and took it as a doctrine, and those who did not He verifies their belief and accuses them of what they are innocent of.

He said: So I said to them: They say: The reason for their saying this is that God has two eyes, two hands, a face, a leg, and a side, and that It comes in shadows of clouds, because it was spoken by the Qur’an, and that is not the apparent meaning of the wording, and everyone assumes that on the apparent meaning of the wording. They believe that God has eyes, hands, face, side, limbs, and organs, and that His essence moves. They curse Him and declare Him to be infidels. So if they disbelieve those who believe this, then their opponents do not have the right to force them to do this after they no longer believe it.

They said: And so are we Christians. The reason for our saying: God is three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, is that the Gospel speaks of it. What is meant by hypostases: other than composite persons, parts, and parts, and other than that which necessitates polytheism and polytheism, and by the Father The son is other than paternity and filiation through marriage, procreation, intercourse, or intercourse.

And everyone who believes that the three persons are three different gods, or three agreed gods, or three composed bodies, or three Separate parts, or three composite persons, or symptoms, or powers, or anything else that requires combination, multiplication, and differentiation. And resemblance, or the filiation of marriage, or procreation, or intercourse, or intercourse, or the birth of a wife, or from some bodies, or from some Angels, or some of the creatures, we curse him, declare him a disbeliever, and criminalize him.

And if We curse or declare a disbeliever to the one who believes in that, then our opponents do not have the right to bind us after we no longer believe in it, even if they bind us to polytheism. The simile is for the sake of our saying: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Because the apparent meaning of this requires multiplication and similes, we also obliged them - we - to use anthropomorphism and similes because of their saying: God has two eyes and two hands. And a face, a leg, and a side, and that His essence moves from one place to another, and that He ascended to the Throne after He had not been upon it, and other than This is something that apparently requires anthropomorphism and simile.

The answer is in a number of ways: One of them is that it should be said: He who believes in what the Messengers brought and said what they said without distorting the word or its meaning. There is no denying this, unlike those who invented sayings that the Messengers did not say, but rather they contradicted what they said, and distorted what they said, either verbally or verbally. And the meaning, or just the meaning, this deserves to be denied by the agreement of the sects.

The origin of the religion of Muslims is that they describe God as He described Himself in His Books, and as His Messengers described Him, without distortion or And without adaptation or representation. Rather, they affirm for him - the Almighty - what He affirmed for Himself, and they deny from Him what He denied about Himself. In that regard, they follow the sayings of His messengers, and avoid what contradicts the sayings of the messengers, as the Almighty said: {Glory be to your Lord, Lord of Might. They describe} [Al-Saffat: 180] that is, what the disbelievers who oppose the Messengers describe. {And peace be upon the messengers} [Al-Saffat: 181]
Because what they said was safe from shortcomings and defects. {And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds} [Al-An’am: 45].

The messengers described God with perfect attributes, and freed Him from the shortcomings that contradict perfection, and freed Him from being like Him in any of His attributes. Perfection, and they confirmed the attributes of perfection in detail, and denied representation, so they provided detailed proof and general denial.

So whoever denies about Him the attributes that He has affirmed for Himself of attributes, then He is a disruptor, and whoever makes them like the attributes of created beings, He is imitating, and the one who disrupts worships Him. Nothing, and the actor worships an idol.

The Almighty said: {There is nothing like Him} [Al-Shura: 11] and it is a response to the one that is similar, {And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing” [Al-Shura: 11] and it is a response to the obstructive one.

The messengers described him as being alive, far above death, all-knowing, far above ignorance, almighty, powerful, mighty, far above incapacity and weakness. And the lowly and the frivolous, Hearing and All-Seeing, far above deaf and blindness, Rich, far above poverty, Generous, far above stinginess, Wise, Forbearing, far above Abstaining from foolishness, being truthful and free from lying, to all the other qualities of perfection, such as describing him as being friendly, merciful and gentle, and God Almighty said: {Say He is God, One - God, the Eternal, He neither begot nor was begotten - and there is no one equal to Him} [Al-Ikhlas: 1-4].

Al-Samad is a name that includes affirming the qualities of perfection and denying shortcomings. He is the All-Knowing and Perfect in His knowledge, the All-Powerful and perfect in His ability, the All-Wise. Perfect in His wisdom.

We have a simplified work explaining the interpretation of this Surah, and another explaining that it is equivalent to a third of the Qur’an, and we mentioned the words of Muslim scholars from The Companions and Followers regarding the meaning of “Al-Samad” and that most of what they said is true, like the saying of those among them who said: (Indeed, Al-Samad is the one who has no cavity) and whoever said Among them: (He is the Master whose dominion has ended) as it was said: (He is the One who is independent of everything else, and everything else is in need of Him) and as it was said: (He is the All-Knowing and Perfect in His Knowledge, and the All-Powerful and Perfect in His Power) to all other attributes of perfection.
And God Almighty mentioned in this Surah that He is one who has no equal to anyone. Thus, He denied that any of the things had equals to Him, and made clear He is one without equal.

And He said in another verse: {So worship Him and be patient to worship Him. Do you know a name for Him?} [Maryam: 65] And He said: {There is nothing like Him} [Al-Shura: 11] And He said: {So Give examples to God. [An-Nahl: 74] And He said: {So do not set up equals to God.} [Al-Baqarah: 22]
Whatever is stated in the Qur’an and the Sunnah proving the attributes of God, the same is stated in the Torah and other books of God.
It is a matter on which the Messengers agreed, and the People of the Book are like Muslims in this regard.

If that is the case, then in their honesty they did not say what Christ and the prophets said, but rather they created a belief that is not found in the words of God. The prophets. In the words of the prophets, neither Christ nor anyone else, there is no mention of the hypostases of God, not three or more, nor a confirmation of three attributes, nor Calling something of the attributes of God a son of God or a Lord, nor calling his life a spirit, nor that God has a son who is a true God from a true God, is The essence of his father, and that he is a creator just as God is a creator, and other sayings containing types of disbelief, which were not transmitted from A prophet among the prophets.
So they said in the law of their faith: We believe in God the Father, the Owner of all things, the Maker of what is seen and what is unseen, and this is true.
Then they said:

And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the one Son of God, the firstborn of all creation, begotten, not made, true God from true God, from The essence of His Father, Light from Light, consubstantial with the Father, by whose hand the worlds were formed and all things created, who for us - the community of men - and from For the sake of our salvation, He came down from heaven, and was incarnated by the Holy Spirit, and by the virgin Mary, and became a man, and was conceived and born of Mary. The virgin, and he suffered, was crucified, and was buried, and rose again on the third day, as it is written, and ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of his Father. Ready to come another time to judge between the dead and the living.
We believe in the Holy Spirit, the Giver of Life, and the Spirit of truth who proceeds from His Father, or who proceeded from His Father, the Spirit of Him who gives life.

So where in the words of the prophets is it said about any of the attributes of God or of His creatures: He is a hypostasis, and that He is true from a true God, from The essence of his father, and that he is equal to God in essence, and that he is the Creator who created everything, and that he sat at the right hand of God above the throne, and that he is the one who He will judge among the people on the Day of Resurrection?
Where in the words of the prophets is it said that God has an eternal son?
Who is the one who named the words of God, His knowledge, or His wisdom - a child of Him or a son of Him, or any of His attributes as a child of Him or a son of Him?
Who among the prophets said: He is begotten, and yet He is ancient and eternal?
Where in their words is there that God has a third person, who is His life, and He is called the Holy Spirit, and that He is also a living and life-giving Lord?
If the Christians believed in the texts of the prophets, as the believers believe,
They were not to blame.
Whoever objects to the texts of the prophets, it is due to corruption of his understanding and lack of knowledge.
But they invented sayings and beliefs that were not stated by any of the prophets - peace be upon them - and they contain clear disbelief and clear contradiction.

If it were assumed that they meant a correct meaning by it, no one would have invented a statement that had not been brought by a prophet that indicates contradictory disbelief. The one who contradicts the law and reason, and says: I meant a correct meaning with it, without his word indicating that, so how, when what is meant is Do they explain their speech as corrupt and contradictory, as mentioned above?

They invented reprehensible statements and interpreted them with a reprehensible interpretation, so the response to them was from both sides, and in this they are equal to Some Muslim atheists who believe in the divinity of some Ahl al-Bayt, or some sheikhs, and describe God with attributes that He has not uttered. Book, and these people are atheists according to Muslims.

Unlike the believers who believed in God and His messengers, who believed in what the prophets said, and did not invent sayings that He did not bring. The prophets, and they made it the foundation of their religion.
The second aspect: That it be said: What you mentioned about the Muslims is an obvious lie about them.
This system that they mentioned is not in the Qur’an, nor in the Hadith.

No famous scholar among the Muslim scholars is known, nor is any famous sect of their sects, who would utter the statement that he narrated about Muslims, as they said about them: (Indeed, they say: Indeed, God has eyes with which He sees, and two hands which He spreads out, and a foot and a face which He turns to all things. A place, and a side).
But these people combined the words of the Qur’an through their poor behavior and understanding, in combinations that they claimed were used by Muslims.

There is nothing in the Qur’an that clearly indicates what they mentioned, for God - the Most High - said in His Book: {And the Jews said, “The hand of God is bound, bound.” Their hands and they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His hands are spread out; He spends as He pleases.} [Al-Ma’idah: 64]

When the Jews said, “God’s hand is tied,” they meant that he was miserly, so God denied them in that, and made it clear that he is generous and not stingy. So he told that his hands were spread out, as he said: {And do not let your hand be shackled to your neck, nor spread it out completely, lest you remain blaming. distressed} [Al-Isra: 29]
What is meant by the extension of the hands is the generosity and the giving, not the abstract extension that they imagined.
Since giving with the hand was done by extending it, it became known in the language to express giving by extending the hand.
When the Jews said: (God's hand is bound) and they meant by that that he was miserly, God denied them in that, and made it clear that he was generous and glorious.
The proof of the two hands for him is found in the Torah and other prophecies, as it is found in the Qur’an.

And agree with them.

Then it is said secondly: The Muslims used the terms of the texts, and you used the terms that were not mentioned in the text.
Muslims associated these words with what the texts stated in the denial of representation.
And you did not associate with your words anything that negates what you have proven of the Trinity and the Oneness.
Muslims did not believe in a false meaning.
And you assumed from the trinity in the hypostases and the union what is a false meaning.

And you changed from this to this.

And you established a law of belief other than what the Messengers brought.

And you said something that does not make sense.

Then you say: He is the Word of God and His Spirit, and then He is two hypostases, a hypostasis of the Word and a hypostasis of the Spirit, but to you He is only a hypostasis. One.

And you say: It is the word of God and His spirit, and the word and the spirit are two hypostases.

And you say: He is the Creator of the world, and the Creator is the Father, and you say: He is not the Father, and you say: A true God from a true God, and you say: A true God. One is equal to the father in essence.

The most important thing you have is what was found in the Gospel of Matthew, not the rest of the Gospels, which is that Christ - peace be upon him - said: (Baptize people in the name of the Father. And the Son and the Holy Spirit).
You have learned in the words of Christ and other prophets that what they mean by the Son is the attribute of God, not his words, knowledge, or wisdom.
And by the Son they do not mean: true God from true God, nor to be born, ancient and eternal,

They do not mean by the Holy Spirit the breath of God’s life, nor do they mean by it that He is a living Lord, but rather by it they want kingdom or what God sends down upon hearts. His prophets and pure ones provide guidance, support, and the like.
The Holy Spirit will be with you and among the Muslims in the prophets and others, as it was in David and others and it was in the disciples.

If it were assumed that the term “Son” was found in the words of Christ, sometimes used in the word of God, sometimes in His human guardian, and sometimes used in the Holy Spirit. Then you assert that these attributes are hypostases, and that God has no intrinsic or essential attributes or the like except these three. Then you separated into three. To other sayings that are long.

Oh, I wish I could see, what did Christ mean by the word “Father, Son, and Holy Spirit” among these matters about which you disagreed? If that was what he meant. What do you claim from the hypostases?

The hypostases - in word and meaning - are not found in the words of any of the prophets. Rather, it was said about them: It is a Roman word, which they sometimes explain. Sometimes by the original, sometimes by the person, sometimes by the essence and the adjective, and they explain it sometimes by the specificity, and sometimes by the adjective.

And if you spoke these words and said: We do not understand its meaning or its apparent meaning is false, and it has an acceptable interpretation, as you narrated it from If you imitate the Muslims in that He says it in the attributes - this would be closer to analogy.

Seeking temptation and seeking its interpretation.

Or they say: We and the Christians agree that we do not contradict the words of the prophets with rational similes, but we followed their words. The clear and abundant arbitrator, whose words there is no contradiction with.

And the extremists among these whom the imams of the Muslims and the majority of them who speak about them declare as infidels say: God will descend to the earth. This saying is not more surprising than the words of the Christians who say: He is the Christ, and that divinity and humanity are united.

They said: The jinn may reside in the body of a human and speak on his tongue, but they are two essences, two wills and two natures, with no union between them. But he entered into it and spoke in his own language.

The Christians say: The Lord of the worlds united with humanity. Some of them say: One essence, and some of them say: One person. Among the extremists of the anthropomorphic Jews is the one about whom it is said that he said: “Indeed, God wept over the flood until it turned red, and the angels rebuked it, and that He regretted it.” (Until he bit his hand and blood ran out of it), and this is clear and clear disbelief, but they say: Our saying is better than the saying of the Christians, for the Christians say: (He was taken, beaten with whips, spat on in his face, thorns were placed on his head like a crown, and he was crucified between two thieves, and the most heinous things were done to him. The law of their faith indicates that, and it is necessary for those of them who deny that, for it goes along with the saying of the unity that is necessary for their sects. Then, what they said about the multiplicity that necessitates contrast, and that one of them is not characterized by what the other is characterized by, and that what happened to it is not permissible to it, It would be contradictory to this.

So their best condition is for them to contradict oneness, just as they contradicted the Trinity, and this is the truth of the saying: These people speak of disbelief. And with what contradicts it, and with monotheism and with what contradicts it.

It is known that what he does to himself, such as remorse, crying, and sadness, is less than what his enemies do to him, such as beating, slapping, and making... The thorns on his head, and his crucifixion between two thieves, and his cry for help for someone to save him from that is more lacking than his remorse and sadness.

And if they said: He did this so that His servants would learn to imitate Him - would those infidels who embody God be able to say: He cried and regretted it and bit his hand in regret? Until the blood flowed, so that he would teach his servants to repent from sins.
In short, no people of that religion said a word about God except the words of the Christians that were more uglier than it.

For this reason, Muadh bin Jabal - may God be pleased with him - used to say: Do not have mercy on them, for they have reviled God as no human being has reviled them.
